[u] Lists: [/u]
[b]Positives:[/b]
[list]
[*] Tension. Remember Tension? What the series feels like it was missing since Resident Evil Revelations 1 and Resident Evil 4? Yeah, Resident Evil 7 has it. Not just jump scares. No, there's actually good tension building.
[*] Synergy. Each element of the game does a pretty darn good job of working with the rest of the elements here: like they actually fit together like a puzzle. One helps the next one, and it delivers a better overall experience.
[*] The Bakers. The antagonists are definitely the highlight of the game, as they provide a skin crawling unease due to their transformation,and how the elements of humanity are still definitely in them. 
[*] Controls are where they need to be for a game like this, although I will recommend a controller ONLY BECAUSE it gives you less control (and that's good for a horror game). But even with a keyboard, there's enough give to make enemies a bit of a problem to hit. 
[*] Great level and scenario design. It plays on your expectations and forces you into new situations that may make you panic. It understands pacing, it understands how to mess with you, and it  understands how to push your buttons. That's a good game.
[*] The visual presentation is fantastic. The one primary job of a horror game's presentation is to set the atmosphere, and RE7's delivers it in spades, with good lighting effects that make you really feel claustrophobia, to great set design with how broken down the house ends up feeling. 
[*] The skin effects need to be highlighted. They really sell the storytelling elements of the transformation of the victims in question.
[*] The story's more personal angle does actually make me more interested then more recent games. 
[*] A great set of PC options to get the most out of your particular build. For the most part, the performance is there as well, hitting 60 FPS pretty consistently.
[*] Great voice acting by Ma and Pa in particular that do their characters justice.
[*] Madhouse mode is a great shake up for someone whose beat the game. It switches things up enough that you feel like the game is new enough, and the new enemy behaviors can really put you on the edge of your seat.
[/list]

[b]Negatives:[/b]
[list]
[*] The last third of the game falls back on the heavy action/enemy sequences of RE5/RE6, and not for the better.  In fact, the philosophy feels so different that it makes me wonder if different teams worked on it. 
[*] No raid/mercenaries mode sorta sucks, but I get why its not there with this type of gameplay.
[*] The music is your typical horror game music: and that's sorta disappointing. Doesn't take advantage of the southern theme at all. 
[*] Couple of bad crashes. Not anything to write home about, but enough where it was like “damn, again?”
[*] Someone has a fascination with remote bombs and the last section is littered with them for no good reason.
[*] Sadly, when the game focuses on the two main protagonists....it gets a lot weaker. They just don't have the intrigue or the energy to really make me want to know more about them.
[*]The connnection to the regular series is sorta weak. I mean, I get that there's some connections, but honestly, it feels like the game's story was adapted to the universe, and was a different story at the beginning of its life. It's a minor gripe, but I could never shake the feeling. 
[*] New engine has one weakness: there seems to be “loading” points that give the engine some problems, where the game actually pauses for a second before continued. 
[/list]

Just a pair of stipulations before I dig into Resident Evil 7 proper – last games I played to any significant degree and finished was the original RE trilogy and I never jumped on the first-person horror bandwagon in recent years. That pretty much made me experience THIS game for what it was without many of the strings attached. In my opinion, at least. In some ways this is both oddly familiar and utterly alien at the same time.

As far as story goes our dude EEEETHAAAAAAAN gets a message from his former wife. Why former? Because, well, she's kinda supposed to be dead. Which really makes it all the stranger when in the message she tells him to forget about her and lead a good life. Kinda sending mixed signals there, aren't you Mia? Following the clues Ethan heads for Louisiana and the Baker family's home where she's apparently at... where he promptly goes through a horrific experience as the hillbilly cannibal family imprisons him and it's not looking so good for the protagonist. Biggest surprise as far the story goes is that, in fact, this whole thing does tie into the Resident Evil mythos but it takes its sweet sweet time getting there and I obviously can't go into spoilers. Not that it's much of a dramatic twist or anything, after all it doesn't take a genius to figure out this ain't exactly natural or what series you're in, but the way story gets there is intriguing enough to keep you invested.

It's also aided by very humorous, disturbing and memorable characters. Mainly the family where Jack stands out the most as he chases you throughout certain parts of the game and you even cross, err, blades here and there. Others have their quirks but it was the father who stuck with me the most and finding out what happened to them and why, doubly so when you get a brief flashback much later on, was the most interesting part of the story for me. It's kinda funny because the entire thing is a footnote in the overall plot. Ethan and other two story-relevant characters are sadly much blander and token. For a regular guy who finds himself in a situation straight out of a snuff movie our leading man sure takes it all in stride. Gotta give that to him at least.

I did like the final cameo of a series familiar character.

But enough about all that fluff nonsense because I know you want to hear what's gameplay like now that the perspective has changed. Well, surprisingly like the olden games from what I could surmise. Sure, it's first-person now and graphical fidelity is way off the charts, but the methodical play style you don't really see much in modern games overall is still there. I absolutely loved the feeling of being stalked in the old house and counting my every bullet, both in how many I had and how carefully I had to aim my shots. Limited starting inventory also adds some edge to this, but I was never forced to play inventory Tetris. One aspect game probably should've handled better are probably puzzles, though. As much as they were basically “Collect a special key to unlock the special door.” and still invoked that “Who in the hell would design this for practical use?”, there just wasn't enough of them as the game is a lot more action-centric now. Thankfully, they aren't nearly as obtuse and contrived as they used to be.

To be fair, I'm speaking from the position of someone who has finished the game – first half is amazing and much better than everything else after you move elsewhere. Claustrophobic and messy rooms paired with enemies that can appear randomly and give chase really set the mood well. This is kinda diluted in the second half or so when you get much more weapons and games forsakes sneaking around to stay alive and conserve ammo for brief, and yes there is a difference, forced stealth section and outright action at the very end. I really do wish it was more evenly spread out, but in a sense that's also staying true because you would accumulate a veritable warehouse of weapons in the old games after a certain point. Not so much in Resident Evil 7 as you mainly get to replace pistol and shotgun for better models, but also get your greedy paws on some specialist weapons like a flamethrower and grenade launcher that will certainly do much good in your hands.

This also brings me to bosses which could've used some more versatility and less of just being bullet sponges. They have far more PERSONALITY as characters than they have mechanical complexity. Just like in the pacing and mood, game tends to make a good impression early on as most of the bosses are in the first half. Final boss, though, was maddeningly a letdown. Come on game, you gave me all this cool stuff and I don't even get to flex my fire grenades beyond stalling for time? Disappointing.

I cannot even fathom how this game has to play with VR on, but even without it was already putting me in that uncomfortable territory. It's horror, alright. Horror relying on jump scares and gore, oh god the gore, but one that makes good use of both of those elements. There are scenes early in the game that genuinely had me thinking I must've failed something, but no and that's just how Resident Evil 7 rolls – one moment you're getting your leg chopped off with a shovel and the next you're putting it together with a first aid med. Outside of combat, even. It seems only the green herbs have survived the Great Herb Wars and they're your primary healing method with the ability to turn them into genuine first aid medicine. I like how everyone's, even your own, ability to heal is actually explained by the story. Nice touch. Oh, there are also collectibles you can find in the form of coins you then use to unlock couple of goodies another character left for you. I'm talking things like steroids to raise your max health, which is still abstracted and tracked by heartbeat meter, and stabilizer to increase your weapon reload speed.

Not being one to really get into graphics this is one of those cases where I have to for couple of reasons. First – game looks positively stunning on higher settings. Effort put into cluttering the locations and making them all disgusting enough to make you uneasy at all times does the other half naturally. Second – it's scalable as all hell and has convinced me Resolution Scaling needs to be a thing in every game. It's nice being able to play the game on a system below minimum specs even if you have to sacrifice eye candy. Soundtrack left me mostly ambivalent. It's your horror soundtrack with situational stings and cinematic score where fitting otherwise, but nothing that stuck with me. I won't be humming anything from this one, I'm afraid.

In the end, I liked it. Is it perfect? No, especially when it drifts away in focus after you change locations, but most of Resident Evil 7 is really good and its well made as a game. Tension and dread are there in almost every hesitant step you make, gameplay is “tanky” enough in first-person to not be so off-putting to me, if that makes any sense, and the mystery is decently engaging. I just wish the main character's motivation came more to the fore and he wasn't just going about for the sake of advancing the story or become someone tells him to.

A warning about this "review", I obsess over certain details of game design, so this will rather be a list or every little thing I dislike about the game, it won't really help someone make a decision whether to buy it or not. There's also some [b]spoilers[/b].

Movement: 

-You can an only run forward, not backwards, left or right. it's more realistic I suppose but I value control over realism, I would have prefered to move at full speed in all directions
-You're always going to want to run, holding a button for that should not be necessary,  a option "always run" should be available.

Aiming:

-For a more classic RE feel, I would have rather not be able to attack unless aiming, then have the aiming be regular walk speed (aiming movement speed is slower than walking) and not zoomed in.
-Recoil and accuracy mechanics are present and I dislike those, I would have prefered for the camera not to move when you shoot and the crosshair to stay static (when you shoot while aiming, the crosshair becomes inaccurate and you must wait a moment for it to be precise again).
-When aiming with the shotgun, the the circle crosshair will induce you in error because your spread as much larger than it.

HUD:

-You have a ammo counter but not a health one, you're forced to check your watch to know your health and it is not very precise. Adding a health counter would also solve the problem below.
-If you are not on full health, you will have blood on your screen, it's very annoying, there's a option for there to be less of it but it's not enough, I really wish I could turn it off completely. Since you stop in place when you check your watch, it's unfortunately kind of necessary (also for the beginning when you don't have that watch yet).

Enemies:

-Some parts of the game don't allow combat and force you to use stealth.
-This is a bit hard to explain, there are parts of the game when fighting bosses go as usual but some others when they always return. In RE3, you'll face Nemesis a few times, each time you can run away or fight him, if you defeat him, he will leave a item as a reward (on normal difficulty) and not return until the next encounter you have with him. In RE7, if you fight Jack in the garage, he will be defeated like you expect but when you fight him in the 2nd floor, he'll stay only temporarily down and always come back, you cannot take your time exploring and you'll burn your ammo. Another time this happens is when you're fighting Marguerite in the Greenhouse (Old house), if you fight her in the 2nd floor, she'll always come back but if you're in the 1st floor (exactly the Greenhouse room) then she'll die. 

Visuals:

-I always seek visuals to be the clearest possible, the only exception is removing shadows, aside from that I try to get rid of effects as much as I can and there are no options to remove fog, "eye adaptation" or the VHS low quality (oddly enough, one tape when you play as Mia as no VHS effect)

Miscellaneous: 

-Holding down the attack button doesn't attack continuously (except for the flamethrower and machine gun)
-The "stash" doesn't stack all items, for example: chemical fluids never stack, medicine stack to 3, handgun ammo to 30, it justs takes space for nothing, all items should stack to up to a 3 digit number
-Cannot skip cutscenes (except those at the very end)

Conclusion:

What really ruined this game for me is the forced stealth segments, the bosses that only stay temporarily down, the blood on the screen (along with not having a health counter). Aside from what I mentioned above, the rest of the game is pretty good, I'm not sure why RE7 is so similar to the 1st one though (I'm not complaining).

The horror...the horror...and I gotta say...IT'S ABOUT FECKING TIME, CAPCOM.

   First up, there's been an awful lot of conjecture about what this game's main influences may or may not have been. From someone who's actually seen an awful lot of horror films, and played an awful lot of horror games, here's my two cents on the subject:

Early Resident Evil games (especially the original) = obvious significant influence;

Outlast = obvious significant influence;

The Texas Chainsaw Massacre movies (especially the original) = obvious significant influence;

The Evil Dead movies (especially the original) = obvious significant influence;

The Saw movies/games = obvious significant influence (towards the end of the game);

...and maybe a wee bit of F.E.A.R., Alien: Isolation, Monstrum, and Penumbra (by the very, very end of the game).

   Yes, the P.T. demo probably played a part in Capcom's decision-making process, but the "influence" here is far more business-based than aesthetic. Konami famously "ripped off" Capcom many years back with a little franchise called Silent Hill (you P. T. conspiracy theorists may have heard that name somewhere), so perhaps Capcom are merely returning the favour since Konami so spectacularly dropped that particular ball.

   Now that crap's over, let's get on with the actual review.

   For a company which has made all the worst possible decisions in recent years - Resident Evil 6, crappy console ports with zero customer service, those appalling c-grade Milla Jovovich action movies - Capcom has finally made one of the greatest decisions in the history of video gaming. Yes, it is my opinion that this entry firmly returns the series to its horror "roots". Sure, they've added first-person to the equation - which they've done a few times before, for the record, just never in a "numbered" RE game - but the spirit of the earliest Resident Evil games is definitely alive and well.

   This game always faced something of a dilemma in regards to keeping both fans of the OLD Resident Evil happy and fans of more RECENT Resident Evil product happy...and it's gotta be said that while it obviously couldn't please everybody, it does have some fairly eloquent solutions to this problem. While the game does a great job of emulating the vulnerability and "puzzles" of the old games (minimal ammo and healing; a shotgun-related puzzle lifted almost wholesale from RE1), it also finds ways to make certain situations fairly "modern" and action-y without taking too much away from the intimacy of the story and environments (just enter the garage for the first time, and you'll see what I mean)!

   The "main hall" of the farmhouse even has faint echoes of the original RE's iconic mansion, without ever compromising the freshness and integrity of the new environments which the game takes place in (while franchise newbies can just enjoy the story and scenery for what it's worth, without needing any prior knowledge whatsoever of RE history).

    Needless to say this game isn't "perfect". The gore is, upon occasion, a tad on the silly side, drawing things a bit dangerously close to "comedy" territory; and the graphics might take a bit of tampering to get them looking just right (amateur "pro" tip to those as clueless as myself: changing my "render" mode from Interlaced to Normal seemed to do the trick, transforming a slightly "blurry" experience into one of the most gorgeous and photo-realistic games I have ever laid eyes upon). But these are minor criticisms at best, cited by a long-term fan desperate to look just the tiniest bit "objective" (when in reality, he's as happy as a pig in mud with his new purchase).

   The only remotely MAJOR criticism I would make is that the "stealth" A.I. is a tad on the iffy side, with enemies seemingly ignoring any amount of sound you might make in favour of only visual recognition. But given how few and far between these parts of the game are, it's no biggie. Despite the significant Outlast influence, this game is certainly not trying to take that franchise's place. (Old fans, rest assured: you will get to murder puh-lenty of enemies before the game is done.)

   Simply put, one of the greatest horror games ever made, and a truly unbelievable return to form for the company which so recently gave us the borderline atrocity known as RE6. This game pulls no punches, unless you were crazy enough to expect, say, semi-explicit genital mutilation and grotesque parodies of female childbirth in a Capcom game. You're not THAT silly, are you? Outlast 2 may yet emerge as the "best" rustic first-person horror game to be released this year, but rest assured that Resident Evil 7 will at least run a very, VERY close second.

I've been meaning to write this for about a week now, but keep forgetting. So, the game itself is very, very good. It's not at all like Resident Evil 4, 5 or 6 in the sense that it is NOT an action game. It instead goes back to its roots as a "horror survival" game, and it does it pretty well. Depending on the difficulty, you can easily find yourself without any ammo or health and having to deal with baddies. Learn to get headshots quickly, as the only other way to kill things is to dismember them (Think Dead Space, only headshots are limbs. You can remove their limbs to the point of death, but it takes a lot more ammo.)

The music is amazing. It's atmospheric and fits the situation at hand. The enemies, while somewhat lacking in the variety department, do a good job of keeping you on your toes. Even though there are few different types, with the way they appear or sneak up on you... whew... My first playthrough was definitely a treat.

It also definitely brings back the unlocks and whatnot from the earlier games. An example of this is that you can unlock an item for any future play for beating the game in under 4 hours. Do not let this make you think it's a shallow game; your first playthrough will easily be at least 8-10 hours. We'll see if the DLC adds more playability later, as I don't get it until the 21st due to Sony agreements with capcom, but even without the dlc I still went through the game at least 7 times.

The villains of the game are quite unique. While on the one hand, you see just how twisted and messed up they are. On the other hand, you actually see them humanized and see what they were like up until the current situation thanks to the background story from files. For example, reading Margerite Baker's letter from her doctor about her headaches. It really fleshes out their personalities and makes you believe that they were really people.

There is some bad stuff, as there is with any game release. One of which is a strange variety of bugs associated with the game. One of which is a massive stutter effect caused by something that I do not know, nor have I been able to find any information on, that is only fixed by finding out the exact graphic combination for your personal person. My roommate and I have the exact same computer, made within a day of each other, and he had absolutely no stutter effect whilst I had it terribly. I did a major boss fight literally fighting a frame every 3 seconds. I still played through it twice like that. The entire game. I did fix it eventually by a speciifc graphic combination and setting the game as "High Priority", but if the thought of this being a potential problem annoys you, then you can easily wait until it's completely fixed.

Several different gun types, dark humour such as, and I'm putting a spoiler here in case you don't want to read it, [spoiler] Lucas: "Languuaaage! There are CHILDREN here - somewhere - maybe - I'm not sure anymore... heeeheee!!!" [/spoiler] End result is that if you like survival horror games that have a fleshed out story and pretty good gameplay (learn to block, as it will save your life) then I have to recommend this. Like I said, I played through it with horrible stutter effects twice: the second time being on the hardest difficulty, and I had a BLAST.

This game is awesome and I highly recommend it. It has a decent story, excellent atmosphere and gameplay, and the graphics look great with a bit of tweaking. Many gameplay elements hark back to the Resi 1-3 days with 'find this and put it in that door' type puzzles, inventory/item box management, secrets and the constant feeling that you're just not going to have quite enough ammo.

What makes the game even better is the replay value. In typical Resi style, you unlock certain items after completing the game and finishing various tasks. One of these is Madhouse mode, a difficulty level that not only ups the strength of enemies but also changes the game in different ways to keep you very much on your toes. This is a great mechanism that more games should use and it increases replayability a lot.

The reason I say Capcom 'almost' nailed it is because the game kind of loses its charm towards the end. Overall the final quarter (?) of the game feels more like Resi 4 than 1-3 (although much scarier, I have to say). It starts off slow and creeping, with an atmosphere almost as terrifying as the demo, but towards the end it seems to lose focus on atmosphere and has more of a Resi 4 action feel than what is experienced early game.

This is still an excellent entry to the series. If you are a Resi fan but haven't kept up with it for a while, now is the best time to jump back on the terror wagon.

Into the gameplay itself, it plays in the middle of a tri-angle of being an amnesia or outlast horror, things kind of flying out at you jump scaring you and every now and then a horrid bloody or mentaly disturbed scene that makes you go "meh" but your mother go "that's horrible" and actually be disturbed by it. Then it has a side of classic Resident Evil games making you backtrack through locations in order to gain better items or health, that inventory system that makes you manage your space accordingly, the feeling that ammo is scarce and must be used wisely, the clunky aiming that makes you be percise and bullet spongy enemies that sometimes can take a critical one shot to the head and the satisfication of that one shot, but that one shot is not offten so it becomes something you hope to happen. and then the last part of the tri-angle is puzzles, the game keeps you moving through the baker estate looking for ways to do things properly, the light puzzles with matching a shadow to a painting to unlock that hidden passage like it's scooby doo or something. As a fan of both horror games and films, i've found myself cringing over recent attempts at horror content these past few years, with films using the same played out idea. and over the past few years, the concepts in horror games have been massively stretched out. we're exposed to the same idea of horror over and over again, hordes of zombies/demons being fought off followed by short creepy cutscenes. however other games like outlast, which i do actually enjoy, use jumpscare after jumpscare and the material wears thin. Resident evil 7 has redefined the Horror genre.

Resident evil utilises one of humanities greatest fears, filth. treachering through mould, digging your hand into overflown toilets, having to hear the sound of flies zooming around corpses, creates an aura of disgust and desperation to escape the bakers. it differs from other games attempts of gore to 'scare' players, resident evil does not rely on any type of blood for its horror or fear.

additionally, for once in a horror game, I truly feel helpless. all bosses and enemies are faster than your character, ethan. you can run and hide, but these aren't poorly coded AI's that you can escape easily. the only option to keep the baker family from tearing you to shreds, especially jack, is by playing stealth. yes you may be able to stop him by emptying your entire inventory of ammunition into his skull, but then you only have a few minutes to do what you can before he gets back up.

To add to this point, you aren't overpowered. yes you have a range of guns, but they do not give you comfort or safety, as all it takes is one of the family to come along, then your weapons are useless. the rocket launchers and miniguns you're used to are swapped out by pocket knifes, homemade flamethrowers that use fly spray, and rusting shotguns.
The henchmen in resident evil aren't to be taken likely either, one of these ink-type monsters can take you down on its own easy enough, so don't be getting arrogant around them any time soon.

Also, resident evil has one of the bests features in a horror game i have seen in a while, video tapes. these optional bits of gameplay add more story to the game in a briliant, creepy way. 

Now. the story; spoilers ahead.

You're playing through the perspective as Ethan, an everyday average joe whose wife has been missing for the past two years, and upon recieving a video tape that possibly will lead to Mia's location, you do the normal thing and go after it, completely niave to the horrors instore.

you come to the Baker's residence, a quiet redneck family thats been missing for unexplained reasons for the past few years, seeming that the house is completely deserted, you let yourself in. shortly after wading through the accumalated mould and filth, you find Mia, but something isnt right with her and she attacks you.

After being kidnapped after fighting off Mia by the head of the Baker family, Jack, you wake up at a 'family dinner' with the rest of the Baker's, Marguerite and Lucas. they staple ypur severed hand back on and after a short while, you escape from the dinner.

Upon escaping, Ethan is desperate to find mia and escape from the Baker's once and for all, but somethings not right, the Baker's just wont die, and what are those black ink monsters in the basement, and who's 'Eveline'?

Resident evil's story is one that makes you hate the antagonists, and then sympathise for them massively. the story keeps players gripped and astonished, while making sure that no one see's the ending.

The multiple endings of the game means players endings can differ slightly but not so much that the experience is completely different.

Overall, Resident Evil has quickly become my favourite game this year and potentially of all time, with the dlc looking amazing, i crave to see what else this game has in store.

Here's my Resident Evil bonafides: the first one I played was RE2, and I LOVED it, instant classic.  I then avoided every single one after that due to reviews until Operation:Raccoon City, I don't know what convinced me to take a chance when that one didn't get good reviews either.  OMG that was horrible, I couldn't even finish the first 10 minutes. I thought "I tried to give the RE franchise another chance, but they made a horrible decision in trying to take this franchise into first-person."  I then resumed avoiding all RE games again.

Then this game came out, and the positive reviews intrigued me enough to give it a shot. Even though the way Capcom marketed it reminded me too much of the hype around Operation Raccoon City.  First person?  Uh-oh.  More action-oriented?  Gulp.

Well I bought RE7 anyway, and at first my heart sunk, because getting the game up & running proved an annoying chore that chewed up over two hours when all I wanted to do was begin the game on my precious Saturday.

But I'm so glad I persisted, because I just finished the game last night and it is FANTASTIC. No other RE title has come even close to surpassing the RE2 experience that hooked me originally, but this one is easily my favorite.  The swamps of the Bayou are the best setting for this type of game, just dripping with foreboding. And you find yourself really interested in the story behind the bad guys, they're so bizarre.  I have to be vague because I don't want to give any elements of the story away.

So yes, it is first-person with no pre-rendered backgrounds, but aside from this Capcom is not lying when they say this game truly belongs in the Survival Horror genre.  It does.  The creation of terrifying atmosphere, the sparse but heart-stopping encounters with monsters which betray whether you loaded up with the right loadout at the last storage box, the maps & puzzle solving, the inventory management, are all solid reminders of this game's roots (remembering that the original spawned an entire GENRE so them's are good roots).

So the frustrating bits:
1) At first I thought the game was freezing immediately upon launch which prompted reboots and forum searches and driver updates, but what I learned is that if I have ANY control peripherals other than my xbox controller plugged in, the game accepts NO input whatsoever. The xbox controller won't work. No keyboard or mouse either.  Only solution is to tab out and close the game. This is because I had a joystick and throttle plugged in at the same time.  Took me 25 minutes of troubleshooting to figure that out because I assumed it was a gfx driver issue.

2) The port does suffer a bit from consolitis.  See my Comments below the review for a description.

3) The game does not support 3440x1440 displays, or more accurately, it does not support 21:9 aspect ratio.  You can set the resolution to 3440x1440 in the options menu, but you get black bars on either side of the screen and are really only looking at a 1920x1440 image.

I was going to refund the game over this issue because I will not pay premium AAA prices for a AAA PC game if it does not support at least 21:9, but pleasant surprise, the ultrawide community have created the solution!  I'm using the 3440x1440 .exe and the FOV trainer found here: http://pcgamingwiki.com/wiki/Resident_Evil_7:_Biohazard and I can confirm they work beautifully. The hardest part is knowing how to UnHide your AppData folder, but there I just gave you the question that's going to be on the exam so now you know exactly what to study, har har.

The FOV trainer did not work until I rebooted Steam, so keep that in mind as well.

So yeah, a bit of a bummer that Capcom isn't natively supporting 21:9, and that it reeks just a tad of consolitis, and their software doesn't know what to do when more than one controller is plugged in, but aside from those initial annoyances which statistically-speaking probably don't apply to you anyway, this game is truly superb and does deserve to be considered part of the Survival Horror genre.  I had a blast (and a few minor heart attacks) playing this game and I'm going to back to play it again as soon as I finish this review!

P.S.  My initial review was actually Not Recommended because I had not discovered the 3440x1440 executable and FOV trainer yet; that explains my grousing in the Comments.  I updated my review after completing the game.

Resident Evil 7:
~~~~~~~~~~~~  

It has been three years since Ethan’s wife was presumed dead, so Ethan was shocked when he received an e-mail from her with a video as an attachment. She looked frail and scared and asked to be picked up in a place called Dudley, Louisiana. He had to go and see for himself if his beloved wife had indeed reappeared. That was his first shock. . . wait to see what’s coming next in Resident Evil 7.

Resident Evil 7 is a first person/ survival horror game where you’ll be playing through the eyes of Ethan. 
After launching the game, you’ll be watching a few fabulous cut-scenes about the story. I especially like the drive along the long road in Louisiana before arriving at a scary, old farm. It is absolutely amazing that from the first step outside your car, you sense a creepy and unhealthy atmosphere. 

Now that you are in the house, it’s truly terrifying. You can hear strange sounds coming from every direction, in dark rooms as well as lit ones. AHHHHHH, another cut-scene, where you’ll meet the inhabitants of this strange place; something to remember. 

There are several aspects to this game: discovering the place, figuring out puzzles and, of course, staying alive. As you enter rooms, you will be able to search cabinets and fridges, or spot items such as ammunition, maps of the favourite bed and breakfast (just kidding), weapons and other articles that can be useful in the game. In the early stages, you don’t have much space in your inventory, but you will eventually find additional backpacks which will increase your inventory capacity. Make sure you find the coins; you can use them to unlock some goodies within the game.  The other fun items to spot are the AFL figurines - these little buggers have a shaking head, are very small and can be hard to spot. It took me a while to figure out what the sound was (shaking head). The ammunition is easy to find but in very small quantities, so make sure your shot counts.  You can combine items to create new ones, such as bottles of medicine (you’ll need plenty of those) and ammunition. The game will save as you progress but I strongly recommend that you save it every time you find a room with a tape player (saving spot) – this would be wise.

In terms of enemies, well, there’s the friendly bed and breakfast crew, and these strange black monsters which appear here and there. Some are crawling and others standing tall. Make sure you shoot at their smiles. Then there are the bosses fights, which are quite intense.

The puzzles are fairly easy to solve, in my opinion. You need some special keys to open a certain number of doors, and that’s pretty much it!

Graphically this game is superb; great details, good contrast - faultless, really. The sound is fabulous, too. I did have a couple of performance issues, of crashes here and there and frozen cut-scenes. Using 2X 1080 GTX with their latest drivers - a bit annoying! The other aspect I feel is not realistic is when your character is running; to me it feels weird and looks slow!

Positives:
~~~~~~~  

-	Splendid graphics and atmosphere
-	Great sound immersion
-	Easy to combine and craft new items
-	Good story
-	Achievement and trading cards
Negatives:
~~~~~~~~ 
-	A couple of crashes here and there
-	Running is not realistic to me

I really enjoyed this game; the atmosphere is fantastic, the graphics are superb and I am happy to have this game in my library.

8/10

Very few bugs on Day 1 and the ones that there were, were mostly just hardware issues which is toi be expected with any release really. I look forward to finishing this game and eventually buying the season pass to support Capcom for such a wondrously delightful game.
        Enough said about launch let me get into the reasons of exactly why I for one love this game but also how it might be a turn off to some.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------        
Pros: Absolutely GORGEOUS gameworld that leaves your skin crawling with every corner you turn.
         Every encounter gives you a fuc*ing heart attack. (Not to mention the strokes you have WHILE in the encounters).
         Many many intricate puzzles that can be difficult to solve without looking at guides.
         When they say this is Survival Horror they should have made sure to put emphasis on "Survival" like this, >SURVIVAL<.
         Audio (Sounds, Music, more Sounds) add creepy yet charismatic color to the sketched work of art that is Resident Evil 7. Making you hate yourself for opening up this game yet at the same time patting your back when something avsolutely terrifying happens on screen, making you look like a sadistic fu*k.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Cons: The puzzles do get repetitive (Find stuff, place stuff, find stuff place stuff, ocassionally kill something while screaming, recieve stuff, place stuff and so on).
          Not as many weapons as Hardcore Resident Evil fanatics would like considering this is a Soft Reboot of the Franchise.
          Some audio delays at certain points (Not sure if this has been fixed completely)
          Only 10 hours (Not including DLC)
          Some enemies can get boring considering you can easily figure out the AI's next move
          The damn people who preordered got Madhouse without having to play the on Normal mode, therefore dying alot and complaining of it being to hard. (NO S*IT)

This review is coming from someone who isn't a fan of the Resident Evil series other than the original game. Much of the later games felt weak, often over the top action shooters that had more in common with the poorly made theatrical films than the foundation of the first game. That being said, I initially refused to pay release full price for Biohazard due to the small amount of content; the dollar per hour ratio being unfavorable. But, then I got a nice coupon for the game and decided to purchase it for around 35 bucks. Still, the dollar to hour ratio was high; yet better.

That being said, I found the game to be refreshing on many levels; a positive change of direction for the Resident Evil universe. I only hope this is a continuing trend for the franchise to avoid jumping back into the Michael Bayesque nature of the previous games.

The game includes a mostly stable experience with lags only during the auto-save points if I was moving; but these lasted only a second or two. Only other issue I had was a brief glitch with the mouse, as it stopped working while at the code-key box during the Lucas mission. I had to close the game via ALT-F4 and redo a small portion. Not a huge deal, more of an annoyance.

The environment wasn't bad, had a good ambiance despite the game being on rails; meaning you had to walk X path to X location; as free-roaming was limited within a predefined narrative.

Sound, background music, etc was all very well done and fit the mood of the game well. The end credit song harkens back to old-school Industrial, sung in a haunting voice to pulsing electronic vibes that would make Trent Reznor proud.

The main characters of the film were well done, Jack, Mia, Zoe, Lucas and Ma being great in their respective roles. I felt Ethan was a bit too stoic at times, his emotional responses seeming a bit subdued and underwhelming. I wish they had broadened his relationship with Mia, showing how much they loved each other. It felt a little awkward and cold. The girl, Eveline was underwhelming and not very scary, doing nothing new compared to what was already done by the other antagonists within the game. In final boss fight, infact, was quite dull and fully scripted.

I will say again the voice acting for Mia and Jack was especially awesome ... offering the most memorable scenes and dialogue.

Some of my biggest gripes may be SPOILERS, so if you want ... avoid reading from this point onward.
.
.
.
.
.

I felt the game should not have offered the endings how they did. While the Mia ending was great, the ending selecting Zoe was a waste of time. The entire choice seems tossed in at the end of development as if you choose Zoe, the following scenes are exactly the same as if you chose Mia aside from the final scene on the Copter. Would had been much better if had been done very differently. I mean, WHO in their right mind would NOT choose their wife? Isn't that the entire reason Ethan is even there? Poor Zoe was written off badly and her ending even worse. This is for sure, one of the worse points in the game.

Another somewhat annoying part is the throttle of movement during the game or the removal of palyer control all together in order to force the story. This is done far too often and at least to me, got irritating.

After all, I will still recommend this game and is a good starting point for people unfamiliar with the franchise or just want a good horror game to enjoy. Just, be warned ... you'll be paying 3 to 4 US dollars an hour to play it at full price as the replay-ability is limited.

Honestly, I was positively suprised by this game. I expected this to be a shameless copy of P.T. and Outlast. What we got is a very gritty and interesting game in it's own right. 

The story seems like it only exists to keep the game moving at first but it quickly expands into something interesting that keeps making you ask more and more questions (most of which it eventually answers). There are a few inconcistencies here and there that might slightly annoy you depending on how much you care about a story in games. I for one care deeply for good stories and I can say that this story was all it had to be and maybe even a bit more. You can feel the japanese influences in every dialogue and in almost every encounter. This leads to the game having kind of a unique feel to it. I myself haven't played too many japanese horror titles and I can say that this did feel very strange and unnerving. Most of the voice acting is surprisingly high quality! While there are no notable names in the cast (except for maybe Mia, I swear she sounds exactly like Ashley from Until Dawn!), every role with the exception of Zoe is very well acted. Zoe just struggles to keep up her southern accent and even loses it completely in some scenes. She also doesn't really get human emotions. Mia, on the other hand is kind of my personal favorite, she really shines in some scenes and her emotional acting is on point. I really started to care for the girl after a while.

The gameplay was surprisingly different from other recent Resident Evil titles. You walk around the Baker family estate looking for key items that you need to progress. Most of the time you are relentlessly hunted by family members or other creatures. The gameplay is very well done, this is some of the best level design I've seen in a game in a long time. I've finished the game 5 times now and after the first time, I already had the whole mansion layed out in my head. The game subtly lets you know where to go and what to do without painting important things yellow (*Cough* Uncharted/Tomb Raider *Cough*) which is something I really respect. I just can't stress enough how carefully designed this game is, it's truly great. I also finished the game on madhouse which is a great way to shake things up a bit. Enemies come from different places and are stronger and key items are in different places which forces you to use your knowledge of the mansion to a great extend. There's also lots of replayability because you unlock new ingame goodies (weapons/abilities) for future playthroughs if you do special things. Why don't more games do this? This game wasn't made to buy, play and move on. This game was made to experience and re-experience over and over again. It doesn't just say "K bye" as soon as the credits roll.

The pc port is FANTASTIC! There were absolutely no technical difficulties when I played the game. Considering I played it on release day, Capcom earned my sincere respect for managing to release a game in a more than playable state.  If we're talking graphics now though, it's not the prettiest game I've ever seen. Textures can be EXTREMELY muddy at some points. You'd think they'd atleast render textures that you'll be falling onto with your face first in high quality but no, some of them really look horrendous. (It does succeed in hiding most bad quality textures though since it's so dark) The game also only gives you the anti-aliasing options of either FXAA, FXAA+TAA or (My personal choice) SMAA. All of those are merely post-processing variants, meaning they are not very performance intensive but also not very... efficient. Since you'll be spending most of your time in this game indoors and in rooms, you should be good though. Just don't pick anything with FXAA or the game will become a blurfest. 

On the good side of technicalities, the game gives you loads of graphics options and even a FOV slider! I was personally very happy with the inclusion of a FOV slider since I found it unplayable with a FOV of 70. This comes down to personal preference though. One small detail that I just love to bits is that wounds in this game are actually dynamic. If you get hit in a certain place and don't take care of the resulting wound, you are able to carry that wound until the end of the game! The blood that comes out of wounds is even dynamic and slides down your arms. You can even make it drip from one hand to the other. I'm sorry but this is truly fascinating stuff for me. It just gives your personal version of Ethan a bit more character. Sure, other players might play the same game but you have a battle scar that nobody else has, it defines your Ethan. In contrast to the environmental textures, the characters look amazing. They are some of the most lifelike characters in video games in my opinion and Mia in particular has some really good hair physics going on. (here again, especially when fighting other characters, look at the dynamic wounds! I JUST LOVE THEM!)

All in all, Resident Evil 7 is a great game with a few hiccups in terms of story. The gameplay is top notch with excellent atmosphere and tension. The technical side is a bit flawed in some aspects but delivers a solid package with a few great details. (WOUNDS!!!) I encourage everyone without exception to give this game a try. It might just surprise you as much as it did me. 

Oh and the theme song rocks by the way.

I've had a lot of fun with RE7. The gameplay is a perfect blend of FPS and the inventory management and puzzle solving of survival horror. If you played the Goldsrc mod Cry of Fear, this is essentially the same but improved in every regard, as its made by a triple A studio.

My first playthrough on Normal took me seven (7) hours, which some may consider short for a $60 game. However, with Madhouse difficulty (unlocked by beating the game) and the several New Game+ item unlockables awarded for beating the game under special conditions there is a lot of replay value. I have about 36 hours and 6-8 playthroughs under my belt personally, and I'm still not tired of navigating the Baker estate.

The graphics are absolutely gorgeous when everything is maxed out. The foliage outside in the beginning can look a bit ugly, but with the right settings most of the bluriness is gone, and the graphics shine indoors and in closed environments. However, I personally had rather ugly "splotching" effects on some floors when the Reflections option was set to "On." When switched to "Adaptive" the game for me looked much better.

There are indeed a few jumpscares, but once you make a couple playthroughs you know where they trigger and you can get some pretty funny results when trying to mess with them, like staring towards the corner they pop out of for instance. Most of the actual scare and horror for me personally though wasn't from the jumpscares, but the sound design, enemy design, and the ambient noises of the house. When low on health and ammo, small creaks in the wood floors would make me jump more than any of the "jump scares."

If you're skeptical if this is worth $60, download and try out the beginning hour demo for free. The gameplay is much of the same, but with much more space/levels, enemies, puzzles, and etc. It's a pretty good little snippet of the game to see if it's something you might be interested in.

This is coming from somebody who never played a Resident Evil game prior to this one.

When I was younger I never liked scary games. However, when I came of proper age, I appreciated them quite a bit more. In fact, it is now one of my favorite genres.

I picked this game up expecting it to be somewhat like PT (remember, I didn't know much about Resident Evil), and in the very beginning I was very happy with what I purchased.

However, that changed when I got my first gun. I thought it would change the game extensively. And it did, for the better.

The combat is fantastic. You need to make EVERY SHOT count. It turns ammo into something you really need to manage.

The scares definitely go full throttle in the beginning, and fade out as the game progresses. I really appreciate how it didn't keep going for the same scares over and over again. The game is still spooky in the later stages, but you have a good idea what is going on so the lightening on the scares is a very good call.

The story was very good. Sometimes a little predictable, sometimes it takes you by complete surprise. A very good balance in my opinion.

The characters are all unique and the levels you find them in all match them perfectly.

Graphics are very good. Some shadows kind of seem strange (gtx 1060 6gb with i5 OC at 4.0 ghz for reference). However; designs, asthetic, and textures are all very solid.

Overall, this game is an easy 8/10.

Wow... Now THIS is one hell of a way to make a comeback! I did not expect Resident Evil 7 to be that great of a game, let alone an awesome and terrifying excperience! Never thought I would say this... But, Capcom, you've actually managed to make a good game and, most importantly, a Resident Evil game that truly feel's like a Resident Evil game. Horrifying... Disgusting... Clever... Tense... Hectic... And fun!

The first thing I wondered before I started playing the game was if the shift from third person to first person was going to ruin the game... And after completing the story, I can confidently say that it actually helped with the atmosphere, the suspense and the combat. A risk Capcom took that, I think, payed of quite well. You never know what to expect with the cramp rooms and corridor's with the first person perspective. The first person view also makes enemies feel much more threatening and ten times scarier.

The enemy design is also really nasty and nightmare inducing. All the family members look utterly insane and loathsome, and when you try to fight them in ther final stage of mutation, their fear factor goes up to like 101/10 (especially Marguerite, she became straight up nightmare fuel). All the versions of the Molded are grotesque to, they're some sort of mix between the regenerador's (one of my favourite monsters from the franchise) and the Leech zombie, which got me super scared when I first encountered them in the first mold room I encountered and the basement. The only problem I have with the monsters is the fact that the variety isn't that great. It's either the family or the Molded, but most of the game, It's the Molded (and I'm not counting the insect minions Marguerite controlls, even though that part of the game scared me the most ;_;).

The story is something I also loved with this game! It's a classical Resident Evil like story with a corperation making a bio-weapon that they lose controll of and make's the whole situation go south. BUT, this time, you don't play as a soldier or agent. No, instead, you play a civilian, named Ethan Winters, who's looking for his wife Mia, who's been missing for 3 years. It all lead him to Dulvey, Louisiana and a big mansion that belongs to the Baker family. I won't tell you what more happens, you just have to figure it out by yourself :)

Thanks to the RE Engine, the environments look super good, the gore, mold and all other disgusting things look super detailed and the sounds are nearly flawless and almost always startling. The combat system is puneshing but also satisfying, rewarding you but also having you on the edge the entiere time. The weapons are extremly satisfying to use and every weapon has it's use. Inventory management is also present, and safe places, with an eerie, but also comforting, melody in the background that reminds you that here, noone can harm you. All safe places have this box where you can store all your items if you don't need them right now, but maybe later.

The soundtrack is amazing... Enough said!

If you do that, the in-game cursor stops working and won't work unless you press shift+tab again. Nothing game breaking, but not to fun either. The other one is when a Molded just walks into a wall without changing directions. It actually helped me when I was scared by making me laugh. But other than those, I've not noticed a single bug.

Summary: To me, this has to be one of the best Resident Evil games in a looong time. With what I mentioned above, it's nearly flawless, from the design of the monsters to the sounds to the gameplay, to even the notes scattered around. Which is why I'll give this game a 9.5/10. GO... BUY... IT!!!

I hate to be that hipstery f*** you'd run into at Starbucks or something, but I was hating Resident Evil before it was cool. See, I genuinely don't like most of the franchise. I can respect, for instance, that most of RE1 was revolutionary for its time - but I don't feel it exactly holds up today. I can admit that RE4 is brilliant, and deserves its place amongst the best, most timeless games ever made.

Here's the thing, though. I, personally, could live without pretty much every other game in the series. RE2, 3, 5, and 6, which account for 2/3 of the core series to date, honestly don't do anything for me. Because I hate myself or something, I have played nearly every RE game, trying to prove myself wrong, and understand the big draw to the series. It's generally just slightly campy pseudo-horror, with passable at best controls and dialogue ripped straight from a bad translation of a 1990s horror cartoon. I include Revelations 1 & 2 on this list, as well as the DS ones. I've been trying to make this work for years, assuming my distaste for the series is somehow my fault, as they generally are beloved by horror fans.

RE6, especially, was so bad it actually contributed to my depression. That isn't hyperbole or a joke - the realization that I had spent $20 on a game that bored me literally to sleep actually deeply saddened me. I was making minimum wage at the time, and had sacrificed nearly 3 hours of my life to purchase that garbage. It was soul-crushing, and I vowed never to buy an RE title again.

But I digress. I bought another RE game. I am the human equivalent of those lab mice that eat the poison repeatedly until they die.

[h1]So anyway, RE7 is actually good.[/h1]

RE7 is basically an attempt at repeating the magic that made RE4 great. It's a recognition that RE6 was ghastly, and an apology, by way of for the most part existing outside of RE entirely. The core series DOES play into RE7, but it's more of a passing reference than deep connection. RE7 might as well be part of a totally new franchise.

It looks great, which is the first thing I noticed. Capcom have finally decided to construct a game that rivals the best-looking titles of its generation, as they did with RE4. Reflections and lighting are remarkably strong, and texture work/modeling is currently unrivaled by any other horror game I'm aware of. If you wanted to s*** yourself whilst pushing your shiny GPU to its limits, this is a surprisingly good game for that. It ran perfectly on my system, to boot. That's sadly always worth a mention, as every year optimization for PC seems to get worse. *looks at Deus Ex: Mankind Divided*

RE7 rips off most of its ideas from other, successful projects at a quick glance. It reminded me a lot of Alien: Isolation with worse AI (fortunately, I might add - A: I had ridiculously great AI - har har). Thing is, by the end I was able to recognize that I was playing a Resident Evil game, so SOMETHING must have gone right. The game manages to have a distinct feel once you get past the first few hours. 

(Side note: The game does a rather clever thing where it outlines clues about your environment rather organically you showing you playable VHS tapes of the exploits of previous residents to the Baker Estate. I just think it's a neat mechanic, and wanted to pat Capcom on the back for it. That's all I suppose.)

It's far from combat-free, and generally works fine as long as you aren't playing on a gamepad - I had some issues aiming with a controller, as there's no aim assist of any sort. My uncoordinated fingers cannot aim a gun with console controls for the life of me. I confirmed this was the issue by trying KBM in the last area of the game.

The plot is bizarrely solid for a Resident Evil game. The writing in RE has never been this strong, and the reveals, predictable though they may be, are entertaining regardless. Critically, the sense of dread the game manages to build is legitimately effective. I was never paralyzed with fear, but I spent most of the game uncomfortable.

RE7 runs out of ideas by its end, and perhaps the feel of the combat could be retooled - running and gunning is borderline impossible even when it feels like a reasonable approach. There are also lots of little details that would have been nice. In particular, the game often plays out jumpscares with NPCs that magically teleport into the corner you were already looking at, but the game assumed you weren't. There's loads of nitpicks like that I could share, and that slightly detract from things.

That said, considering I wasn't expecting anything decent at all, the fact that RE7 is actually kind of great really drives the point home that there's a reason it's a household name. I might not "get" the series as a whole, but if this is the same feeling fans originally had towards RE1, I understand why some defended RE6 years later. Well, not really. But still.

After the truly abysmal sixth entry in the main series, the Resident Evil franchise was in need of a much needed revival and Resident Evil 7: Biohazard more than delivers. Picking up the remnants of the sadly cancelled P.T. and turning it into their own game, Capcom have proven in this that they can, and will, scare the ever-living crap out of us.

In a first for a Resi game, this is played entirely in first person and if you have it on PS4, you can use VR. While I would have loved to play this in VR it's unfortunately not out on PC yet, nor do I have one. However I was able to run this at a smooth 100fps on ultra and apart from the occasional hitch when loading a new area, I had no framerate issues. And the game is drop dead gorgeous on the highest settings, there were times I just had to stop and look around because of how amazingly detailed everything looked.

The story itself, at least the first half, is very Texas Chainsaw Massacre-like, with you exploring a dilapdiated house inhabited by a family of "hillbillies", but in reality, they're not hillbillies, in fact the Baker family are a rather wealthy and intelligent family who simply had the misfortune of being at the center of this biohazard.

And my god they are terrifying, the father, Jack, is a walking tank, smashing through walls like they're made of paper, ripping the hood off a car and being shot, set on fire and blown up and yet he still keeps coming at you. His wife Marguerite is nowhere near as aggressive, fleeing if you shoot her enough and easy to avoid but the insect swarms she sends at you can be irritating and halt your progress, and then there's her later form which is nothing short of horrifying, looking like a spider wearing the skin of a human, her boss fight is one I was more than glad to be done with. Their son Lucas never attacks you head on and instead settles for a Saw like torture room in which you have to solve his puzzle or risk death. It was a nice change from the usual fare of unloading ammo on them in the hopes for a break and also made you think. Finally we have your wife, Mia, she really only shows up as a boss for the first hour or so and is easy to beat but I'd be lying if I said she wasn't creepy, especially when she crawls up a darkened staircase at you. Oh and I guess I should mention Zoe, the Baker daughter, she really doesn't do much other than help you find a cure, it's a shame as she could have been a great character but was sadly wasted. All the boss fights were interesting and the way you could change the flow of a fight was interesting, and while you can easily trivialise them with the use of the magnum, the ammo for it is so sparse you'll be stuck with your usual weapons most of the time.

While all the boss fights were great, the last one was.... well let's just say it was disappointing, consisting of you walking towards them while blocking to prevent being thrown back, hitting F to finish them and then the 2nd and 3rd phases both consisting of you merely shooting them while being held upside down, even if the weapon you get for it is cool.

The main character you play as in this, Ethan Winters, while he's not the worst character and certainly not the worst voiced, you can't help but feel that he seems to be going through the motions in this, he never really seems scared or phased by anything. Hand or leg chopped off? No worries, he'll just pour some medicine on it. Crazy woman becoming a spider thing or an old man crashing through a wall and soaking up bullets? Doesn't matter to him. It's possible that he's an Umbrella agent or someone with experience with biohazards but still, at least show more emotions than the basic ones.

Sound direction in this game is some of the best I've heard in a horror game in years, the slightest creak, footstep or breath had me frantically looking around for the source, most of the times it turning out to be me unintentionally scaring myself. The music adds to the urgency of an encounter, especially the sharp stings when being chased that seem to literally stab at the eardrums, heightening the fear and causing you to panic. This game is definitely best experienced with headphones on and the volume cranked up with the lights off.

The puzzles could have been better designed, to be honest. Sure, they weren't overly complicated with an inexplicable solution but they were a little too easy, especially considering I was going in blind, the longest I spent on a puzzle was at least two minutes because the damn shadow wouldn't rotate the way I wanted it to.

Few weapons but the ones that are there are all rendered in amazing detail and have their own unique feel, the magnum, flamethrower, and grenade launcher in particular had a really nice satisfying feel them as you unloaded them onto an enemy and watched them stagger back in pain or their head pop from the damage.

Small variety of enemies, there's really only the Baker family and the Molded and some insects in one section but they provided enough of a challenge as is, and the Molded in particular are creepy and require planning to take down swiftly, but they sadly show up way too often in the later game and you can easily just run by them. The game could have been even better with the addition of at least one more enemy type.

There are side stories in the game that are provided by files found throughout the game and do an excellent job at providing backstory as to what happened to the Baker family. There's also the VHS tapes that are optional but are best played regardless as they can show you a solution for an upcoming puzzle and provide a viewpoint of another character, usually one who has no weapons and thus has no choice but to hide and avoid combat.

As expected of a Resident Evil game, there's a fair bit of backtracking but exploration is encouraged and rewarded quite fairly, and if you want that magnum later on in the game then you better get to looking for those antique coins.

After the horror that was Resident Evil 6, I was wary of this when it was first announced but after playing it and absolutely loving it, it's definitely up there with Resident Evil 4 for me and hopefully Capcom keep this up for future entries.

Resident Evil 7: Biohazard is a survival horror videogame and the latest entry in the famous Resident Evil franchise by Capcom. Althought it takes place after the events of Resident Evil 6, 7 is very different from the previous installments, both in premise and gameplay. You take control of Ethan, an average man, looking for his missing wife in the swamps of Dulvey, in Louisiana. Soon enough, Ethan finds himself trapped into a large estate populated by a deranged cannibal family and hideous, fungal monsters, and must survive an entire night filled with danger and find his beloved.

Resident Evil 7: Biohazard is a very much welcomed return to the survival horror roots of the original Resident Evil games, with a greater emphasis put on exploration and resources management than the big action set pieces and huge firefights of Resident Evil 5 or 6. The gameplay tries to highlight this new direction with various elements:

- An inventory system which allows you to carry with you a set amount of items at a time, with the possibility to store them in and out in big boxes located near save points/safe rooms. While this system can be annoying at a times, forcing you to go back to a safe room just to dump some excessive weight for the new useful/plot-relevant item you just found, the inventory in Resident Evil 7 forces you to consider carefully what to bring with you and what just plain leave behind. A crafting system is also introduced to combine items you can find in the environment to create ammo or healing kits of varying potency

- Ethan is not as durable as an action videogame hero, but that doesn't mean he's defenseless against the hostile creatrures and humans you'll meet: he must dodge or defend himself from attackers and hit them where it hurt the most instead of just spraying them with bullets. While managing your resources in order to have always ammo for something and an healing item to use in a pinch is a vital part of Resident Evil 7, there are certain sequences where you'll have to face proper boss fights or a great number of enemies. In such circumstances, the game takes brief and enjoyable breaks from the survival horror formula to have interesting and believable action sequences. Still, there are certain enemy bosses that can be only avoided via stealth and traps you must either disarm or dodge

- The game takes place in a single, big location (the Bakers' mansion and its immediate surroundings) you'll have to slowly crawl your way into. The emphasis on exploration in Resident Evil 7 comes from the fact that many doors you encounter can only be opened by keys you are getting much later, requiring some backtracking in the process, and, generally, investigating every corner of the environment will make your life easier (not only you'll find more resources, but also special items you can spend to "empower" yourself or destroy to recive NG+ bonuses)

These elements, along with some important story revelations you can experience much later in the game, make Resident Evil 7: Biohazard a brave return to the formula of the original games, but also a Resident Evil game in its own right, with very familiar gameplay elements and ties to the overall narrative of the series. This game is filled with its own original memorable characters too, with the Baker family definitely taking the central stage.

The only minor issues that can be pointed out about this game are the scripted sequences, which tend not to mesh that well with the general flow of the gameplay and, at times, seem to come right off the blue, and the final two levels or so, with the game becoming extremely generous when it comes to resources and weaponry and, therefore, a lot easier, with a disappointing final boss fight at the end.

Resident Evil 7: Biohazard was without a doubt the right direction to push the series forward and a great survival horror game in its own right with a very enjoyable gameplay, oppressive atmosphere, great moments all around and a fantastic direction

Picked this up the day after release and just finished it an hour ago. Here is my spoiler-free review.

First off, the bad: The ending. I won't spoil it, but it is not so fufilling. That being said, RE games were always about the journey so, while a con, it's not one that's out of place. Next is the length, while my first playthrough took 7 hours, it can be completed much faster, going as far as an achievement for beating it in under 4 hours. That being said, if you take your time and explore like you should, it can last you 7+ hours. Finally, the textures. When looking at textures, you can clearly see that is was built with console hardware in mind. This is a con, but also is not. Doing what they did helps by making it accessible to more PCs and a more consistant experience overall.

Now the good: Optimization; I did not have one crash in 7+ hours of playing nor many glitches. Most was a hand sticking through a door when I shut it on a monster. In addition, The visuals and sound are AMAZING. While the textures can be lacking up-close, everything else is gorgeous. Shadows and lighting look stunning and the sound design is absolutely disgusting (in a good way for this game.) Just playing this makes you feel like you need to shower. Next is, the gameplay. Gone is punching giant rocks, back is the tense atmosphere and hightened heartrate. The first person is also something I consider good in it. It doesn't take away anything. At no point did I feel like I was playing something else like Outlast or Amnesia, it always felt like Resident Evil. Puzzles, keys, keycards, and inventory management. Boss battles are here and done in a very Resident Evil way too. The final good thing (hopefully) that remains to be seen is how the DLC is handled. Being that it's already out on the PS4, so far it appears that this wasn't content that was cut and repackaged. It's something that adds to the game, but not to the story (which is how it should be.)

Overall, well worth my money and loved it. It's back to RE's roots in a new refreshing way and earns it's place as one of the better RE games, the best since 4.

I have never played any of the previous Resident Evil games prior to this. So, if you are like me or maybe are a big fan of the series then this review might help you a little! I'm normally the person to shy away from the horror genre but this looked too good to turn down and I'm glad I didn't!

[h1] Review [/h1]

Resident Evil 7 is a first person horror survival game set in an abandoned Southern farm house, which you explore in the perspective of Ethan - the fresh protagonist of this new beginning of the Resident Evil games!

The story is fantastic. From the get go you are immersed and the pacing of both the story and gameplay is perfect. The voice acting is brilliant and the Baker family were so brilliantly done, however Ethan was mediocre at best as he felt like he had no emotion or depth. I wish we had more interaction with Mia and Zoe because I felt like we had only scratched the surface with them as characters. There is so much lore scattered around the map which I found interesting. I really loved the way they have done the video tapes in the game, it adds so much to the story and gameplay (I'll get onto gameplay in a few!) At the end of the game it shows there is a free DLC coming in Spring time so I will be excited to see how the ending develops. 

The gameplay is just outstanding. I love the isolated camera, it makes you feel so claustrophobic in the mansion which is very ironic yet so perfect for this horror survival. Gunplay is superb but limited which isn't much of an issue. You can obtain 3 hundguns, 3 shotguns, a grenade launcher, a flame thrower and a machine gun. Two of the handguns and shotguns require solving a puzzle and finding the very rare repair kits throughout the game. Aiming feels clunky but in a good way, it really adds the panic to the fights. Ammo and other supplies are so scarce so every shot, ever heal and every enhancement counts. Inventory management is great, there are some backpack upgrades throughout however its never enough so item prioritization is key.  The lack of enemies is disappointing but not much of an issue as I still was terrified every time I seen something. The bosses were fantastic, each one was so unique and interesting... The last boss was not a challenge in the slightest but still enjoyable. 

The puzzles were great, some were obvious and some required some looking around but nothing was too hard to find. The video tapes featured puzzles and the way they did them was fantastic - it was more than just watching a cutscene. This game did an awesome job of its map exploration, the game introduced new areas slowly and required you to do some backtracking to unlock new parts of previously explored areas. Safe rooms were brilliant, I honestly loved the breaks from the suspense, manually saving the game and managing my inventory. 

The visuals were insanely good. The dark, gritty feel to the graphics was great yet it looked so beautiful. There were actually a few pretty shots especially the shots in the beginning and end! The enemies were awesomely designed and were so terrifying! The sound was perfectly done. The music changed dramatically from relaxing music in the safe rooms to suspenseful music in the monster infected house. Some of the sounds made chills go up my spine, especially the second boss when they were hiding *shivers*  The environment was so scary, I always felt like I was on the edge of my seat. The game did brilliantly with not over doing jump scares etc and stayed horror filled throughout.

I'm now looking forward to playing the previous games and this could be the start of a great new cast of characters I'm sure for the hardcore fans! Brilliant from start to finish. 9/10
