Just beat this game. Friggin' amazing. Here are some tips and tricks to help noobs throughout the game (I'll keep it as spoiler free as possible):

Don't waste ammo. Especially the shotgun ammo. Instead, when facing against the monsters, Shoot just one of their legs off. Don't bother with the arms or the head, just shoot off one of their legs. then, after they jump at you once to try to attack you, run up to them and do an aim stab at their head, this will often kill them instantly. If it doesn't kill them on one hit, hit them again. (Aim stab: Attacking while aiming with the knife). WARNING! This method does NOT work on the Fattys, youll have to shoot them to death, Though you can still try.

When you are trapped in the garage with immortal joe, go to the table on your right and grab the car keys. I will say nothing more except to not even bother shooting him. But on Madhouse, you will have to grab the lockpick  next to where the locker where the first aid med is, and use it quickly to  open the box that has the car key. You have to be quick. Shooting him too much at this part will make him go into the car and try to run you over. you can still beat him, but it will be much harder, especially if you wasted your ammo on him prior to the sequence. 

When immortal joe is chasing you throughout the house, Again, don't waste your ammo by trying to kill him. Instead, keep running away, and only periodically turn around and put one or two well-placed bullets in his face. This will stagger him, slowing him down so you can run to safety. Also, you CAN hide. Eventually he will stop chasing you and will begin to wander around to find you. USE THIS TO YOUR ADVANTAGE.

Have At least 10 rounds of enhanced pistol ammo (This ammo is only obtained by combining gunpowder and strong chem fluids). Use this ammo for emergencies, or when faced againced a group of monsters. Shooting their legs off will be MUCH easier when using this kind of ammo. Don't use against Immortal joe. Well, you can if you want to, as one shot could stagger him easily on normal. same may go for madhouse difficulty, though I still recommend just using regular ammo to stagger him, no matter if the difficulty is normal or madhouse. If youre on easy, then by all means, shoot away.

NEVER DISCARD ANY ITEMS. If your inventory is full, then take your lazy a$$ to your nearest stash and store your extra items. ESPECIALLY with the treasure photos. there are three of them. If you discard them, it will be impossible to obtain the hidden goodies, despite knowing exactly where they are. On the flipside, you don't need them in your inventory to obtain them, you can store them in your stash and the treasure will still be available to pick up. Up to you, the player, to decide what you want to do with the photos.

Antique coins! you need (Well, you don't NEED it, but it helps) at least 9 coins i believe. The .44 magnum isnt essential, but it is useful in some situations. Trust me, I would know. I beat the game without it. Psychostimulants are VERY rare. But they are useful when coin hunting, or if you want to do one more sweep for items and ammo in an area. Use them whenever you like, but I recommend you only use one in an area (I.E. The house) AFTER all the monsters are dead and immortal joe is no longer able to chase you. You will know when, Don't worry.

Save often. Need I to say more?

Mixing solid fuel with chem fluids makes fuel for your flamethrower, but if you mix the solid fuel with strong chems, it makes grenade launcher rounds. I didn't know this until I tried it. Was forced to live without the flamethrower for some time. Spend/combine your items with care. 

You can repair the broken shotgun using a repair kit. There are two in the game, one for the broken shotgun, the other for the broken handgun. you can find one easily, after you are able to leave the house. Its hidden under the porch inside a box you have to break. I recommend you fix the shotgun first. Why? Well, it does hold only two shells at a time, but does significantly more damage then the standard shotgun. Plus, you will be able to save shotgun ammo more easily. Try to find stabilizers to increase the reload speed, because it is dangerously slow to reload (maybe 3 or more seconds to reload). The other repair kit is hidden, and it requires the third treasure photo with the manniquin head to find it. You can use it to repair the handgun, which holds only 7 rounds but does more damage than the G17 handgun. Fantastic on your first playthrough on normal. You can find the repair kit in the testing area, maybe the second or third room after you find the two keycards. I will say no more.

Resident Evil 7 is a game of references. From the opening shot that is lifted almost directly from The Shining to the last minute cameo by a familiar face of the long running franchise, playing “spot the influence” is an ongoing metagame throughout the entire ten hour long campaign. It's hard to categorize the game as an honest sequel to the storied series; any ties to the established characters or lore are tangential at best and are almost hidden Easter eggs for hardcore fans to dig up. Instead, Resident Evil 7 acts as a greatest hits album of the horror genre in general, and completely abandons any convoluted baggage acquired from over twenty years of fan service in favor of safely bringing the series into the modern horror game landscape. It's not particularly original. It doesn't move the genre forward any great lengths. But it's a damn good first person survival horror game.
 
  I've been waiting for a sequel to Condemned 2: Bloodshot for almost a decade, and Resident Evil 7 may as well be that game. The protagonist is even named “Ethan”... Played entirely from a first person perspective, you spend most of your time rummaging through trash and filth, battling goo monsters and psychopaths in dilapidated environments and searching for supplies to fend off the creepies. Your mission is to rescue your girlfriend from the clutches of an unhinged, cannibalistic, superhuman family that branched off the Texas Chainsaw Massacre genetic tree. Each family member acts as a gatekeeping boss and their personality traits dictate the hazards you'll face in each “level”; the father is a physical damage sponge, the mother is a supernatural stalker, the son likes to play games and set traps like Saw's Jigsaw, and the grandmother is a mental ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. You'll dispatch each of them and solve simple puzzles to unlock wings of the Cajun mansion and some of the surrounding bayou, but the game remains intimate and small scale throughout.
 
  Graphically, Resident Evil 7 is extremely impressive in it's depiction of rot and decay. Even when things get surreal and supernatural, with black slime undulating on the floor and walls and obese zombies projectile vomiting at you, there's a commitment to realism and polish that sells the setting. You can almost smell the rotting food in the cobwebbed refrigerators and being funneled into a realistically flooded basement elicits some real dread. There are filters and effects galore, including taking part in a few found footage style VHS mini-campaigns. Most of the horror comes from visceral gross out scenes, and it's only effective when this much attention to detail is payed to decapitated bodies and spider infested doorways. There's never really a pleasant moment to be had during your visit. The entire game can be played with a VR headset, though I wasn't able to try this (or wanted to, frankly). While I could see how the isolating nature of virtual reality could potentially add to the atmosphere, playing on a traditional television led to some cheesy situations; extended, gratuitous scenes of sharp objects being waved in your face or characters invading your personal space can reek of a tech demo. It's not overly distracting or a game breaker, but it's akin to watching a movie made with 3-D technology in mind on a 2-D set.
 
  You enter the Baker mansion unarmed and vulnerable, but before long you're armed to the teeth with the expected arsenal; an always handy, box-breaking knife, a pistol, then a shotgun, a machine gun, remote detonated bombs, and the flamethrower from Alien: Isolation (you were warned about the references...). Ammo can be scarce and enemies take somewhat random amounts of damage before they go down for good. A single shotgun blast to the face of a standard enemy may blow his head off, or it may just bowl him over. The intentional clunkiness of the combat feeds into the Resident Evil mantra of deciding to spend either health or ammunition to get past a situation, and the save rooms and inventory management are critical to survival. The magic, bottomless inventory box returns from previous games, probably the most overt tie to the series' legacy. Combining herbs to produce healing items is also present, but the mechanics are more complex; instead of green herb plus red herb equals super healing item, you now use a chemical agent to mix with the herb and that same agent can be used in formulas to create handgun rounds or flamethrower fuel. Again, it's that health versus ammo balance. You have a limited number of items you can carry on your person, so there is some backtracking, experimentation, and fiddling involved. Toward the end of the game I was so stocked up on a half dozen types of weapons and items it became frustrating to manage, but again that's one of the most Resident Evil-y things about Resident Evil 7.
 
  Resident Evil 7 is a celebration of all thing horror, which the series kind of was at it's roots, anyway. Part of me wants to... condemn the game for being Resident Evil in name and nebulous themes only, cashing in on the series' history, but I guess I'm not attached to the franchise enough to really care. It may not be the “scariest” horror game out there or the best example of first person story telling, but as a mass market, big budget spooky roller coaster ride it's quite impressive.

Well what can I say, after an era of mediocre 3rd person action Resident Evil games we finally have a return to roots survival horror. Resident Evil 7 isn't perfect but it's exciting, atmosperic, a tad spooky and loves to keep you on edge. I have completed every achievement and have unlocked every secret item and weapon. For those fans of RE this is a must play. If you are a fan of immersive survival horror this is a must play, if you are looking to get into the series this is a must play. 

Content wise you can count the amount of guns in the game on two hands and if you had a friend you can count the other items on 3 hands. However, the game is paced extremely well and there was never a time were I felt the game was getting repetitive. The game brings back some of the tranditional level design long lost from Resident Evil 1 and 2. There are doors locked with emblems of snakes, scorpions and other creatures. You do easy but interesting puzzles to open secret passages. There are tons of notes and journals painting the backdrop of the story and what is happening at the baker's house. 

There are 3 major areas in the game that are seperated by a barrier that does not allow you to return. 1st area is the largest, 2nd is about half that size and 3rd is basically a straight line but still large enough to count. There are only a handful of boss fights but they are done way better then any bossfight previously seen in RE. There are only 2 enemy groups in the game. 1st group has 4 subtypes and 2nd group has 3 subtypes. You will see group 1 through the entire game. This is my biggest complaint of the game. While the enemies still manage to put you on edge to the very end I would of liked to see a couple more enemies groups.

Difficulty wise I have played through the game 3 times one run on each difficulty. I could hardly notice a difference between Easy and Normal. The true way to experience this game is in Madhouse. No checkpoints, limited saves, better item placement, resource management is required and enemies are quicker and have new move sets. This game mode is locked behind Normal mode unless you pre-ordered the game (♥♥♥♥♥♥ Capcom) If you manage to get a hold of a copy with it unlocked DO YOUR FIRST PLAYTHROUGH ON MADHOUSE. You will die...maybe a lot, but it's way more fun.

Overall, this game is fantastic in almost every aspect. It has a clear objective and it succeds. It is a tad on the short side, I finished my first playthrough (on Madhouse) with almost 0 help in about 9 hours but 1st person shooters are nothing new to me. The enemy variety is a little thin but what enemies are in the game hold till the end. I'm also not thrilled with how layed out DLC is. Some of the mentioned DLC could of easily been placed in the base game to make the $60 count. If you are a die hard RE fan or a die hard survival horror fan I could recommend you spend $60 on this, however a wise man might wait for a sale.

Let me just start off saying that this is actually an amazing game -- in its own rite and as a new chapter of one of my favorite franchises. For the first time in several iterations, Resident Evil made me scared s***less. I dreaded playing this with the lights off. There's this sense of terror each time you enter a new room.

That being said, this game tried VERY, VERY hard to keep me from enjoying it. I really wish I bought this for the PS4, where at least it is guaranteed to run like a normal game. On PC (at least for me and many others online), there's a myriad of technical issues. For me personally, the game seems to freeze constantly. It initially started out as a little nagging bug. The game would freeze for 1-5 second intervals every 30 or so seconds. Pretty annoying. But I thought, 'I f***ing love Resident Evil. So I'm going to suck it up.'

For whatever reason, the problem seems to have gotten worse the more I progressed into the game. About halfway through the game, the freezes became much more frequent and longer. I got so infuriated when I kept taking hits in combat because the game would freeze for seconds at a time and when it comes back, my aim and timing is completely off. Boss battles got unbearable in this respect. But by far the WORST are the cutscenes. I do not mince words when I say that there's not a single cutscene that has not been ruined for me. The freezes continued into these cinematics for me. Only in the cutscenes, the frame would stand still while the audio kept running. So there were several cutscenes that would freeze about 2 seconds in and stay paused for the next 20 seconds. By the time the game comes back, I've already heard everything that happens. Whatever surprise or dramatic reveal is ruined. There are entire segments toward the late game that are intended to be scary and suspenseful, but the freezes got so unbearable and game breaking. The game would freeze LITERALLY every 5 steps I took. They became so frequent that I made a game of it -- I would count the number of seconds it would take before the game would come back. In the past hour of gameplay in which I've been playing this minigame, the game froze for an average of 18 seconds at a time, roughly every 2-3 seconds. Sometimes the game would freeze, come back for about a fraction of a second, then freeze again. The longest freeze I've experienced was 55 seconds long. I literally had time to check my phone and reply to a text. When the game came back, I took 3 steps forward before the game froze again.

I'll say it again: This is an amazing game. It's just a shame that it runs like garbage. The game is so unplayable. I should not have to bite my tongue and groan in mental fatigue everytime I load up this game for which I paid $60. I didn't want ot wait for the price to drop because I've been an avid fan of RE since I was a kid. But now I feel cheated. I really, really, really hope that Capcom reads this. This review comes from a long time Resident Evil fan. Played RE since RE1 and they're one of my favorite games. I've liked all of them to a certain extent, even the latest: RE6. The formula has changed over the years and by RE5 and RE6 it had become a lot like a wave shooter where fear and survival weren't really a part of it anymore, it was about over the top action. The games became more about action than survival horror. This was highlighted by the fact that areas were graded and there was even a post-game game called mercenaries that focused on scoring a lot of points. 

RE7 does away with that action oriented trajectory and gets back to the roots of Resident Evil.

Returning to its roots doesn't mean everything is back to how it once was. The most notable change for the series is the new camera perspective. RE7 is a first person game now. I wasn't sure what I thought about this at first, but after playing through the game I can say it works very well and the game always feels like Resident Evil, not some random shooter. This comes across in the enemy reactions to being shot and familiar weaponry. Aside from the shooting there are a lot of other aspects that help it feel like Resident Evil. Familiar items like herbs are in the game, limited saving (on higher difficulty levels), storage containers, inventory management, and easy but fun puzzles. 

Perhaps the most Resident Evil-like thing about the game is the environments. Each RE has always been about a single incident at a specific point in time, usually a short period of time, taking place in a single location. RE7 is no different in that regard. The game takes place over the course of a night at a house. But like other RE titles it doesn't constrain the environments too much, there is a lot of variety, and a sense of progression to more dangerous and interesting areas. 

The story is actually pretty good, and can be looked at in two ways. The first way is to look at it for what it actually is: an infected family is crazy and trying to kill you. The other way to look at it is to think of how it fits into the larger RE universe. Throughout the game the connections are only hinted at through files you read. Most of the game is spent simply trying to save someone, learning about the family that is trying to kill you, and trying to survive. It is only near the end that the connections to known RE entities are revealed.

It's obvious though that with how great the game is that they held back. One of the drawbacks is the lack of different enemy types. There are only really two enemy types in the entire game that you regularly see. A third, and some minor bug type enemies come in once in awhile. Another drawback to some would be the lack of RE universe related story and characters. It's like they wanted to test the formula in the marketplace before committing entirely to well known characters and story elements. 

I think RE7 is great and by the end I was wanting more and I'm excited about future installments for sure. This gameplay and pacing with well known RE characters and storylines would be amazing. This is a very different feeling than I got when I finished RE6. At the end of that I was thankful to be done with it, although I enjoyed it, it was exhausting in how formulaic the game design was: locking you in an arena and sending hundreds of enemies at you. After finishing RE7 I was thoroughly impressed with all aspects of its design and can't wait to see what comes next.

Side Note: I'm glad I was able to play the game from the start on Madhouse difficulty, but I think that should be standard, not a pre-order bonus. I have to say that I might not have liked RE7 as much if I played on normal my first playthrough. This type of game changes drastically with different difficulty levels. On madhouse you can't kill many of the enemies you see, you have to find a way past them and save ammo for bosses. You have to think about if you should save or not (limited to the number of casette tapes you pick up, although there are plenty). I think it is more enjoyable on a higher difficulty as a first playthrough.

It really is the best Resident Evil game since 4, which is amazing since I expected this game to be mediocre when it was first announced. 

The fear is genuine and is built in two ways. First, the amazing atmoshpere and score, which create a sense of dread and danger. Every area of the Baker residence is unique, and present new types of threats and challenges. The environments are interesting and offer a large variety of secrets to investigate. The music, though nothing really memorable (other than the credits theme), adds to the environment by kicking in at just the right moments to add to a situation. Dreadful music for when you're hiding, terror music when you're unexpectedly attacked, tense music when fighting a boss or multiple foes, and so on. 

The second method this game makes use of to create fear is through the enemies. Although the enemy variety is dissapointingly sparce, they more than make up it by being real threats. Enemies are quick, evasive, and deadly. They'll try to dodge your shots, sneak up on you, hide, and even group up. You have to plan out your engagements when you know there are enemies around, as the resource scarity and damage taken to damage given ratio makes it impossible to go guns blazing. If you try to be a badass and fight every foe directly without thought you will die. On top of that there are suprise enemies that force you to be prepared to fight at any time, keeping you on your toes throughout the experience. 

As for the the story, it is fed in bits and pieces, and the connecting dots that are found find keep you interested and invested. For refernce, imagine the mystery and supense of the demo but actually maintained throughout the entire game. I won't spoil anything because it's fun discovering the story while surviving the Baker family, but there's plenty of twists and moments that subverted my expectations for where the journey would go. There are few to no tropes and cliches, which is something that horror games struggle to avoid. On this alone I would recommend this game. 

 It shouldn't be amazing that a game actually lived up to the promise of the trailers and demos, but in this era of buggy dissapointments and rehashed experiences Resident Evil 7 stands out as a refreshing and unique experience that other games are sure to mimic in the future.

Resident Evil 7 is a fantastic entry in the Resident Evil series, and is a must own for fans of the classic survival horror games (before 4). I say this as someone who was very hesitant to purchase this game because all I had seen from the marketing was PT and other gimmicky horror games with little actual gameplay or substance. However, I am happy to say that this is not the case. Resident Evil 7 might be the best entry in the series since REmake. 

In terms of visuals, the game looks fantastic even running at 720p like I had it to maintain a solid 60fps (yes, I know my graphics card isn't the best). I am speaking astetically, the atmosphere and overall look is on-point, however the actual texture work is sub-par on PC according to others. Nothing that will affect your enjoyment though.

The gameplay is really solid. Aside from a lengthy, scripted introductino that does get annoying to replay (I did 3 full playthroughs, one on each difficulty) the game rarely takes control away from you. Most of the time you will be wandering around the Baker property in search of resources, key items to progress, and making the choie to either kill or avoid the Molded enemies that stalk the halls. A fair bit of the game also involves hiding from the Baker family themselves, which is less than perfect. The game lacks any real stealth mechanics to make this a good system, and the Baker's line of sight often makes little sense. Additionally, they tend to teleport around for the sake of bothering you, no matter how immersion breaking it is.

The gunplay is solid, and on Normal difficulty you will find ammo is given generously enough to keep you always armed, but also on the edge of being defensless if you are wasteful. The Shotguns are particularly powerful, as always, and will make short work of the Molded. Most of the puzzles are pretty simple, and this game has a number involving rotating weird objects to create shadows on walls that open doors. Makes about as much sense as any other puzzle in this series. However, there is one particularly good puzzle during the latter part of the game that has a great twist to it. The boss fights are sort of hit and miss here, as one is great fun, one simply goes on for too long (even on easy), and one seems virtually impossible on Madhouse difficulty without using some unlockable items.

Speaking of unlockable, the game has decent replayability as well. At the time of writing this, I have just finished all three difficulties and unlocked all special items in around 20 hours. My first run on normal took about 11 hours, then I completed easy in 3 hours, followed by a 6 hour Madhouse run. There are a number of bonus items you can unlock that will make Madhouse a much more reasonable experience, as without them it can prove to be one of the most difficult Resident Evil experiences. However, unlike Resident Evil 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, Code Veronica, Revelations, and Revelations 2, there are no bonus modes to be found in the base game. Capcom clearly ripped those from the game to sell back as DLC. However, given the quality of the base game I am fairly confident the DLC will be good and I am looking forward to it. Resident Evil has to constantly re-invent itself to avoid becoming too familiar and with it less scary or tense. After classic RE and action-RE, we now have a return to the more survival and atmospheric parts of the franchise.

There is a constant eeriness to the Baker's mansion and surrounding areas. While the graphics might seem weird at first (especially in the daytime opening), when everything gets darker and is combined with the fantastic sound direction, it really sucks you in. I don't remember the last time I was genuinely terrified of going down the stairs in a video game.

Despite the change in perspective and how you interact with the world, RE7 is still very familiar. There are lots of subtle and not-so-subtle nods to older puzzles, but the pacing itself also harkens back to old titles. You are defenseless at the start of the game, slowly move on to better weapons later in the game and have a full arsenal at the end of the game. What sets RE7 apart from the rest of the series is that enemies are far more resilient and you are far more vulnerable, so even if you are equipped with firearms, each encounter may cost a lot of your resources.

It's an excellent game and a fresh approach the series so sorely needed after riding the Resident Evil 4 wave for so long.

So, I just finished this about a minute ago, figured I'd write a review as the game is fresh in my mind. Now the game hours you see here as of January 28th, don't represent the amount that I have actually played rather I also made my friends try the intro and have AFK'ed a couple of times. So, that said, lets get on with the review.

I have been a big time Resident Evil fan since I was a child, I didn't know it yet though and so I was too scared to play them, specifically the 2nd one. Grown up now, I am playing ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up games like this and damn does it scream Resident Evil. Don't let the first person perspective fool you, this IS Resident Evil and it is everything a Resident Evil game should be, is it the perfect one? No. But its a damn good one.

So what is there to expect? This game will get in your face freaking you out all the way through, its a slower kind of Resident Evil but not slow like Alien Isolation, there is stealth in the game but in later half of this game, just chuck it out the window. While there's no zombies there are crazy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ trying to kill you in the weirdest ways while being a walking quote machine. The Baker family in the game have a lot of depth and especially a lot of character to them, they are fun to deal with while frustratingly pants ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ scary. But there's more than just that, its the type of highly memorable situations this game will throw you into involving them and these moments are the only moments you'd see in a Resident Evil game. There are also puzzles and they are so reminiscent of previous Resident Evil games and its not hard to figure out but finding the objects to do the puzzles is the hard part. Now enough of me emphasizing on how much of a Resident Evil game this is.

The game play is first person perspective but its still quite hard to move your character when it comes to the types of situations you're in where you have to dodge, block, escape, and even kill your enemies in the game with this variety of weapons going from the good ol' knife that is surprisingly more reliable to the Grenade launcher that will ignite your enemies. There is still a 180 turn and light jogging which is quite frustrating when your character is so slow that Jack Baker is able to just walk and keep up pace with you, the game again, limits you on how you move adding to the horror of the situation. The controls are pretty solid on controller too, I haven't tried keyboard and mouse yet, but the only complaint I have is that RB/R1 is your healing and when you're in a frenzy and trying to shoot your enemies or even run away, you WILL accidentally hit this button and pour some Jesus Juice on your arm healing anything you want. That is frustrating as hell when you have full health too. Otherwise, solid control. It wouldn't be a Resident Evil game without some sort of crafting system and so you can make Jesus Juice from the green herbs (No Red or Blue herbs this time, Racism, amirite?) and 2 forms of chemicals, Yellow stuff which is lower quality and red stuff which is stronger. You can also use these chemicals to make a variety of ammo, the only ammo I didn't see included was the shotgun ammo, no spoilers here ammo or 44. Magnum ammo. But you have basic handgun ammo to Grenade launcher rounds.

The game has a deep atmosphere too it, they range from creepy to plain disgusting and my opinion of the game's graphics won't matter much since I played on low settings on my weaker laptop to achieve roughly 40-60 FPS through. The game does run great, a whole hell of a lot better than Resident Evil Revelations 2 which was like running Mario 64 on Sega 32x. I was happy that Capcom finally delievered a decent PC port of the game with a surprisingly large amount of graphical options. Good on you Capcom. The game looked fine on low-ish settings though and I didn't run it at full Resolution (1920x1200) but close enough. The sounds as well are haunting and can even make you jump when its just a normal usual sound. This game makes it so much harder to move around area to area when you think you're getting stalked every second and for being a Resident Evil game, this has surprisingly good voice acting. I know that times have changed and voice actors actually take their job seriously but this is an A+ effort for voice acting and therefore makes the situations in the game all the more believable.

Now do I recommend this game, yes and I recommend it if you're a newtime fan. This game makes subtle hints from the previous games and I do mean subtle but there are a couple easter eggs here and there with even movie quotes from other horror movies but honestly, this game is a big departure from the last two games while being set within the same universe as the rest of the games.Now this game's length is fairly long, ranging from 10-12 hours. I completed it in roughly 10 hours in one playthrough. This game is wonderful and doesn't take itself too seriously but isn't too silly either, its a good combination of the two and if you are a die hard fan like me, you won't be disappointed.

Like Resident Evil 4 before it, RE7 looks to rejuvinate the series with a rather dramatic change in gameplay. Moving from 3rd person to first person, the game looks to give an immersive experience close to the feeling of the original four games (1, 2, 3, and C:V). Does it succeed?

Well...yes and no.

**WARNING: MINOR SPOILERS IN THIS REVIEW**

RE7 feels like what The Evil Within was attempting to be. If you take TEW, FEAR, Silent Hill and RE and smash them together, this is pretty much what you get. It shines in certain areas and fails in others. 

The graphics are great. The landscape is detailed and it really helps immerse you in the game. I never really got tired of being in awe of how the game looked. The atmosphere is perfect and the areas are very reminicent of the original Resident Evil.

That being said, performance leaves a lot to be desired. Multiple times the game dropped frame to the point I thought the game crashed. It eventually moved again, but it happened more times than I expected from a AAA developer. It's especially a problem when your trying to deal with enemies. It happened most often in the Main House and Old House areas.

Enemy density feels just right. They aren't too numerous to be tedious or overwhelming, but aren't too sparse either. They aren't super tough, but will mess you up if you aren't careful. The guns feel satisfying to use and the crafting does what it needs to without feeling pointless or too complicated.

Now, for some of the things I think hold the game back:

The length. It's short. My clear time was about 8 hours. That feels far below standard for a 60 dollar game. Not only is it short, I pretty much found all the secrets and collectables on the first play through. There isn't a lot of replay value. Most of the secrets aren't all that impressive anyway.

The story. It started out fairly strong, but went off the rails after the 2nd area (The Old House/Greenhouse) and never recovers. It's full of plot holes and unanswered questions (ex. whatever happened to Lucas after he runs off?). The entire ending feels like a rush job. On the whole, I was very disappointed.

The main character, Ethan. He's bland and boring with no background. With any luck, we won't be seeing him again (or at least hopefully he gets some development in the future).

Thus, we come to how I rate it. The problem is it barely has any ties to the rest of the Resident Evil franchise.

If it was called anything else, I would probably rate it 7/10. 8 if I'm feeling generous. As a Resident Evil game, I have to give it a 5/10. 6 at the best. It's too disconnected from the rest of the series. It's still a better game than 5 or 6 was though.

Either way, I can't recommend the game for the price of 60. When it goes on sale at $30, yes, definetly grab it. Until then though, save your money. Maybe they will fix some of the performance and story problems in the future.

Resident Evil 7 is the bastard child of RE1/2's item management and exploration, RE4's gunplay, Amnesia's puzzles and enemies, and Outlast's immersion and gore.

When I began the game, I was pretty sure I was playing Outlast at first.  The first hour or so looks and plays a lot like it.  Eventually I received a pistol, and that's when I really understood why RE7 stands out from other current first person horror games.  The gunplay is fantastic and panic inducing; missing three shots on a monster that is barrelling towards you makes you feel like a true loser, not only because you are now being anally penetrated, but now you wasted three bullets AND you have to use your only medkit.  Aiming and firing is very similar to RE4.  Walking backwards while looking down sights reduces movement speed to a disabled turtle crawl, forcing the player to take potshots at enemies until they are close, then pulling a 180 and sprinting away to fire more shots.  Enemies lose body parts depending on where they are hit and can be used strategically.  It makes every encounter matter, and forces the player the use some fight-or-flight tactics throughout the game.

I don't believe the story is too short.  That seems to be the main gripe with many reviewers.  I believe a longer story would have begun to drag on for too long.  I really recommend playing through the game at least twice.  There are end-game unlocks depending on your playthrough stats that can be used on the next playthrough.  Also, Madhouse difficulty not only makes enemies harder, it also moves items to different locations.  I figured that would mean that you would find ammo in new places or something, but during a boss fight a key I needed was in a lockbox that I needed to pick.  On my first playthrough it was just on the table.  It's a good way to experience the game again and I highly recommend doing this if felt like the game wasn't long enough for you.

TL;DR: it's kinda like Alien: Isolation but much, much better.

It's strange, but there's nothing to compare RE7 to. It's a true survival horror: it has shooting, hard enemies, puzzles, items and inventory. But we haven't had a real survival horror in years! All horrors we've had over the last years either had no puzzles, or no fights (just running away from invincible monsters), or... well, no horror.

Imagine Call of Cthulhu had puzzles. Imagine 85% of Alien: Isolation gameplay wasn't built around one single invincible monster that does the same things over and over again. Imagine you could fight the enemies in Amnesia: The Dark Descent. RE7 sums it all up and does it better.

It takes all the best things from previous RE games, and it'll satisfy both new players and fans of the olden days. Challenging difficulty? Check. Save rooms and item boxes? Check. Creepy mansion? Check. Classic puzzles with keys and locks? Check. Ammo and healing items crafting? Check. Scary monster attacks! Check. It's all here. And more!

It's an extremely engaging game, emotionally powerful and amazingly directed. When I first launched it, I couldn't stop playing for 3 hours straight while saying 'Oh my God" and "What the f**k" (I meant that in a good way) out loud every few minutes. Which isn't something that happens to me often.

And on a side note, no, it's not just an attempt to make a mysterious scary game. It's scary sometimes, in a true Resident Evil way (like a huge monster crashing in through a window), but it doesn't just throw otherworldly FNAF-like jumpscares into your face when you simply turn around the corner. It's a world where you can fight back in a proper survival-horror way.

Resident Evil 7 is a funny game to review. On one hand it feels like the most “Resident Evil” game in a long time, on the other hand it really doesn’t stand up to even RE6. 

Visuals and sound in RE7 are outstanding save the firearms. You really do feel as if you’re in Louisiana on the bayou fighting for your life against insurmountable odds. They do an outstanding job of instilling fear into the player at least until story and gameplay issues creep in.

The story starts on a contrivance and ends on one too. Ethan the story's main character hears from his wife who has been missing for three years. On a whim he leaves for Louisiana in a coupe wearing a button down shirt, slacks and square toe shoes. He arrives at a dusty looking mansion deep in the bayou never thinking that he should be prepared for anything. In every other RE that is a part of the numbered series the heroes come at least somewhat prepared carrying a pistol at least. And by the way the game ends Ethan should have known better. Things in the game kind of just happen and there is no real flow. This is made clear by the fact that someone calls you on conveniently placed phones to tell you what to do next right as you complete the previous objective. This happens through most of the game then the main villain reveals them self in a most predictable matter. After that you spend the rest of the game tracking down the big bad, kill them and the game ends.

Gameplay is a bag of cheap mixed nuts. Bad jumpscares, good jumpscares, a pedestrian set of weapons, puzzles for the sake of puzzles, backtracking for the sake of backtracking. It feels like the game is checking checkboxes more than trying for a cohesive experience. It’s like the devs think players liked RE1 for the jumpscares, puzzles and backtracking alone so put them in the game even if it doesn’t make sense. To be fair some of all the above are good but others are there just because. Weapons suck for the most part but I'm cool with this because it makes sense in this game because you are supposed to feel helpless. Also the first person prospective fits the narrative.

I will give credit when it’s due, Capcom put a lot of effort into RE7 and it shows but I feel that they need to tighten up the story and gameplay. 

[b] Buy if you are a RE fan, buy on sale if you are not. [/b]

Let me preface this review by disclosing the fact that I am a *relative* newcomer to the Resident Evil franchise, I say this because I have not played any of the games before RE4 save for the REmake on gamecube.

I, Like many others, noticed a steady downward trend in quality from 4 onwards. I witnessed what could best be described as a series undergoing a serious case of identity crisis. 

Was it a horror game with action elements?

An action game with horror elements?

An interactive Micheal bay movie with a few jumpscares?

No one knew, least of which capcom.

Thats why It is so refreshing to see Resident Evil back to its roots. Do not let the first person perspective fool you, This is not P.T., this is not your average Early Access walking simulator. This is the closest we have come to a faithful, wholesome Reimagining of the first RE since the actual HD remake. 

First of all, the mansion itself, the location you will be spending roughly 70-80% of your time in. It is filled with tons of secrets, puzzles, and survival items hidden away in all of its revolting nooks and crannys. From the various pieces of lore scattered around to the hidden crafting components you would need to be hopped up on stimulents to catch (which thankfully, you are able to craft yourself). There is much to see and explore within the baker family residence.

The Combat is remarkably weighty and satisfying. Everything from the standard pistol to the homemade flamethrower has a tactile and visual  effect on enemies. When you shoot an abominable humanoid bio weapon in its "Head" with a round of buckshot at point blank, it just feels good. So good in fact, that it might be working against the game in a way, at least in my own personal opinion. I was not dreading encounters with the Bakers, or various adversarial organisms, i was looking forward to them. I felt powerful and deadly with my arsenal, and at no point did i feel that I was mistaken with this perspective, even in the games boss battles which are, admittedly, the weakest part of the game.


As for negatives in the game, by and large I was left wanting more after my 16 hour playthrough. I wanted more of the hefty, tense combat and the eerie unsettling atmosphere. I also found the experience, at least on hard difficulty, to be rather forgiving and generous on ammo and healing items. Lastly, I did find the way through the game to be fairly linear, at least, more so than RE1 Which I feel is what this game is very much trying to emulate.

In the end though, despite these flaws, this is the best Mainline Resident Evil title to come out in a VERY long time and should appeal to those who have waited so long to experience such a title.

Feels like a soft reboot of the franchise with a much bigger focus on horror. Gameplay-wise there's a lot of features returning from classic RE games: save rooms with item boxes, you can investigate items by rotating them and discover new uses or items that way, backtracking after discovering key items, and there's a bigger focus on resource management. But key differences include the first person perspective, a completely new cast of characters, and a generally darker and grittier approach to horror (unlike the extremely campy, action-style approach to horror the series always had).

Playstation 4 version of the game supports VR, and you can tell there's several scenes in the game which were designed specifically in mind for VR. PC version has no VR support whatsoever, which seems like a strange omission. What the game does feature, however, is one very valuable lesson about marriage: don't chase your spouse with a chainsaw. And the game features a handy "I'm scared!" mechanic mapped to LB on gamepad.

The way the game is designed reminds me a lot of DmC. It's a new direction for the franchise with the gameplay feeling different and familiar at the same time. If you've been wanting a break from the over the top storyline, action gameplay, and empowered characters of recent RE games, and you want to play as a relatively fragile main character who encounters a family with a serious domestic violence problem, then this is the game for you. I'm a total wuss when it comes to actual horror and family drama, so this wasn't my cup of tea.

They brought back the creepy mansion setting and made it scary and challenging in different ways than the horror masterpiece that the original RE is. Unlike Outlast, there is fighting in this game. Lots of shooting monsters here. Lining up head shots is a must for success.  
In parts, RE7 is actually scary. The beginning of the game wasn't even really fun. It was distressing how uneasy, even spooked I felt playing through it. My nerves were definitely on edge. The mood and tension are set immediately. Then the game moves in to the more typical classical RE game play of solving puzzles, finding keys, and blasting away the creatures that stand-in for zombies. As the game progresses, the game gets less scary. It kind of becomes predictable when you are possibly in danger or not. However, there were still some times when I hesitated to proceed because I knew there was some spooky horribleness in store for me if I go into that room. There's a lot here of what made the RE series so endearing in the first place. Stylistically, this game couldn't be further from RE6. It's a return to the classic RE style of games mixed with the modern champs of actually scary horror games, Amnesia and Outlast. The boss fights are all with members of the family. Speaking of which, what's up with little girls as the main villains lately. Revelations 2 did that and now we see it again in their next game. Also, there's a really bizarre fight where you have to shoot a woman's crotch that has a big bee hive on it.
I gotta say, the ending of the game was weak. The ending just kind of snuck up on me. The big reveal of the identity of the villain behind it all wasn't surprising at all. Also, the final boss battle was insultingly easy. I set a couple bombs off in front of it and unloaded my machine gun on it until it died. It seems like a fast and cheap version of previous RE final bosses that was phoned in. The game took around 10 hours to finish on my first play through on the hardest setting available (Normal) from the beginning. The game time was significantly shortened because of the auto saving. No need to really ever go reload a save while you're playing because when you die the game usually puts you back to somewhere really close to where you were. Overall, this game is really impressive for striking that difficult balance of brining back the old style of RE game play while adding new twists; all the while keeping the game moving along at a good pace. It was a fun experience and I definitely recommend Resident Evil 7.
Update: The Madhouse Mode that's unlocked after beating the game should definitely be played as well. It significantly ramps up the challenge and makes the game scary all over again, just in a different way from the first playthrough. Also, the unlockables in this game are really fun that make your character very powerful so subsequent play throughs are much easier. It make achievement hunting very accessible and fun. The DLC is decent (Banned Footage Vols 1&2 so far). There's a lot of bite size stuff here that offers a good variety of game play styles. Ethan Must Die is probably my favorite. Finally beating that after sooo many attempts was extremely satisfying.

[h1]Go Tell Aunt Rhody that Resident Evil's Dead[/h1]

Well where to begin with this travesty? If you're a long time fan, I'm talking 20+ years balls deep in to this franchise, chances are, you're older now and have more of a brain to use, therefore, critical thinking should come a lot more naturally and effortlessly to you... That being said, I'm going to be rather blunt in my criticism of this game.

If you're a teenager who gets all emotional and butt hurt when someone tells you the truth, you need to either take your blinders off and grow up or just leave now before I rain a hellfire of truth upon you.

[h1]Is this Resident Evil?[/h1]

To put it succinctly, no, no it's not. Let me explain. Puzzles, inventory management, clunky controls, item boxes, weapons and saving data on outdated recording devices aside... This game is missing some major key elements plot wise and theme wise in order for it to be considered Resident Evil...

First of all, the most obvious thing to note is that this game is not based on Zombie movie horror tropes any longer. Instead the director decided to shift focus to the Evil Dead, Texas Chainsaw Massacre and Saw franchises for inspiration. If you were expecting zombies, rabid zombie dogs, crows, Tyrants or even a familiar face then forget it because any of those elements I just mentioned are non-existant in this entry to the series.

Why people say this game "goes back to it's roots" is beyond me, aesthetically speaking, yeah, sure... there's a spooky house... is that what it takes to be Resident Evil? Hardly. At the core of it all, it's not doing anything remotely simliar to the original 3 (or 4 if you count Code Veronica) Resident Evil games. 

The entire time I played this game, I thought it was a really interesting horror game, but as a Resident Evil title it basically ♥♥♥♥ the bed. I understand that a lot of people will argue that Resident Evil hasn't been itself since Resident Evil 4, and I have to agree but at least RE4, 5 and 6 had the recurring characters which is the only real thing that made it Resident Evil...

In all honesty, renaming The Evil Within to "Resident Evil" would have been closer to the mark than this game and Evil Within had really no resemblance to Resident Evil either... It could ha worked based on what they did with this entry in the series though.

[h1]One Step Forward, Two Steps Back[/h1]

While this game is a technical marvel and the graphics are amazing, there are some major overlooked flaws that need to be addressed. The horror atmosphere is there, the inventory is there for the most part, and the game is creepy. However, I found myself more frustrated with this inventory system more so than the past Resident Evil games, even though the "mansion" in this game is about a fraction of the size of older Resident Evil titles... 

In fact, it's probably the smallest RE game to date design wise, but the inventory system is just obnoxious as hell. Why you ask? Because some items stack and others don't. Any kind of crafting materials you find don't stack, keys no longer remind you that "You no longer need this key, would you like to discard it?". 

Video tapes and pictures are now a part of taking up inventory space. Even after you watch certain videos or look at certain pictures they remain in your inventory unless you full out discard them or throw them in your item chest. Keys need to be placed back in your item box as well or they forever take up space even after all their associated doors are unlocked. I thought to myself, why is this even a thing? Even Resident Evil 1, the grandaddy of all inventory micro-management had better quality of life mechanics than this brand new 2017 entry... How the hell is this even possible? *facepalm*

There's 4 available hot keys to swap weapons on the fly, however you can also put healing items and other stimulants to buff your character in these slots... Do they actually work when you press the desired direction on the D-pad though? Hell no they don't... Why do they allow you to hot key items you can't use on the fly? 

The first time I died in a boss fight was because I tried to hot key a herb and then frantically mashed the d-pad to use said herb and my character didn't do anything... The game doesn't even explain the rules of these hot keys at any point either... They just assume you're going to use them for weapons only.

Again, a very counter intuitive design for the inventory, it's a bit convoluted and hazy, the only real way to understand it is through trial and error and I find that to be laughable at best all things considered... like this game being made in 2017 and it being a triple A title. The Inventory in RE1 is more self explanatory and to the point than this is, and that thought alone is scarier than any monster you'll see in this game.

[h1]Final Thoughts[/h1]

I'm going to recommend this game as a good survival horror game but not as a Resident Evil title. As a Resident Evil game it gets about a 3 / 10 from me as it's not Resident Evil... Honestly Resident Evil 6 was more of a Resident Evil game than this is and that's just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sad because I HATE RE6 with a passion.

In good conscious I can't recommend buying it at the ridiculous price tag it has currently and for those of you that went out and bought 3000+ dollar rigs to play a game that runs less than 10 hours of total time on your first playthrough, you just got sucker punched in the nuts by life and Capcom... I hope you learned a valuable lesson.

As a stand alone survival horror game with no ties to the Resident Evil franchise, I'd give this a solid 6.5 / 10. It misses the mark in a lot of ways, the controls are terrible as far as FPS standards are considered, the strafing is just abysmal. The meat of the game is all scripted boss encounters with no real enemy threat to face. You always seem to have enough resources to deal with the small amount of monsters they throw at you.. and btw, all the monsters are basically just re-skinned regenerators from RE4... another uninspired trash idea from Crapcom.

Don't buy this at full price, don't expect to be blown away by this entry either. In typical RE fashion the game starts out really strong and ends on a wimper that feels rushed and forced. No one at Capcom knows how to write a cohesive story that has a strong finish... There will most likely be a couple sequels to follow running on this exact same engine as it just opened up a whole new series of plot holes (to be expected) and of course Capcom has to milk it for every penny...

Also the whole first person perspective is just complete garbage... I wish they made it an option instead of forcing us in to that perspective. I felt it took away a lot of what made the old Resident Evil games scary. I enjoyed watching my character almost get killed by an advancing enemy as I ran down a hallway in the opposite direction... In Resident Evil 7 there's none of this, you basically just turn your back and say "Whatever I can't see, won't hurt me" and proceed to bolt down a hallway, quick turn and close the door behind you.

All in all, I'd suggest waiting for a sale, and run the game on medium to high settings, it still looks great. I ran this game with a GTX 970. i7-950 on medium / high and it didn't look any different than those running it with the recommended settings... 

I'm sure some edges could have been a bit sharper but all in all, the game looks fine running on the minimum requirements. Considering it's lack luster approach in trying to excite all of us, it failed miserably and isn't worth emptying your wallet for.

If you're a die hard fan (like me) and must own this game, try to find it cheap (like me) or wait for a sale. My true final verdict is to avoid this game completely and wait for the Resident Evil 2 remake as it will most likely be a better game than this, the most obvious reason being that Resident Evil 2 is actually a Resident Evil game where as Resident Evil 7 is not.

I'm not a big fan of Resident Evil.  I have played all of them though except 0, which I own just haven't played.  I appreciate the games, even 5 and 6 to some extent because no matter what kind of the game each installment wants to be, they succeed at it.  6 was a pretty decent action game, 5 was a pretty good co-op game etc.  I was very much looking forward to 7 because the demo was a nice showcase of some of the gameplay and aesthetics of the full game and I have to say, my expectations were exceeded. 

Not only is this a very great game on it's own when not compared to its predecessors (despite some questionable scares like jumpscares or loud noises startling you instead of general ambiance), the game feels, plays and IS a perfect marriage of some of the best parts of each particular Resident Evil game that came before it.  The first third of the game plays almost exactly like the first game, as you search a run down 'mansion', the "invincible" Bakers who stalk you in the halls of the houses are very reminiscent of 3, and the combat is almost directly carried over from 4, where firing at particular parts of the enemy causes different senarios for the player to exploit the enemy easier.  The last third of the game is more combat-centric without completely diluting the horror aspects which could be tied to the more combat heavy 5th and 6th entries in the series.

The world building is very detailed and cared for.  Proper lighting and very detailed enviornments do a lot towards making the enviornments you run around in feel as unsettling as possible.  The character writing is very well done too.  I was hesitant when the protagonist had a voice, because voiced protagonists rarely fit the tone of the game or they become rather annoying with their constant talking to themselves during certain story bits.  In RE7 however, Ethan is quite reserved in his speech and when he does speak he speaks when it is appropriate to and some times interjects some dark humor into the game.  As does Jack.  Jack is probably the most memorable character next to Ethan due to his appearance and his (unintentionally?) hilarious dialouge during chase sequences/boss fights.  It's great to hear him and he is well acted as well.  The same generally goes for Marguerite and Lucas as well.  Each are well acted and well written for their characters to make them threatening as well as sympathetic.  

The story seems to be kind of contrived at first glance, as the prologue does not give very good first impressions on the rest of the game, but given enough time (basically just past the prologue), the story becomes rather interesting to uncover and there are a few twists that may not exactly shock you but are appreciated and can lead to theorizing about what really happens behind the scenes.  

Resident Evil 7 may be first person, but it is most definitely an RE game at heart.  The game is fun to play, has decent replayability, several difficulties and lots of secrets to uncover with a great story and cool characters.  If you were hesitant to play it before, it's totally understandable, but if you like RE or horror games then you should feel right at home here.

As this is my first foray into the Resident Evil series, my perspective may be a bit different than many of the other reviews you find here. 

I found this game enjoyable, but only just so. The game is not impressively long, taking me about 8 hours to beat after a single start over maybe half way into the story. As a very scripted game, I also doubt that I will find myself playing through again absent some significant DLC making it worth my time. 

That being said, the atmosphere is truly unsettling, the mystery is compelling, and the characters are perturbing. As a series newcomer, I wasn't quite sure what to expect. The pacing is very slow, but deliberate. You move slowly, you aim slowly, you open doors slowly, but this adds to the realism and suspense that will keep you playing. The game takes some classic scare tactics, throws them in with a believable atmosphere, to create a genuinely suspenseful experience. Only once or twice does it manage a fright that will set you back in your chair and bring your partner crashing into your gaming room with a prop katana, but it will still give you enough consistent anxiety to make playing a thrill. 

The survival and crafting elements are not the focus of the game. They add something, but not much. There are all of about 8 things you can make in total, and many are simply an upgraded variety which consume rarer resources than their more basic counterparts. These resources are difficult to come by though, and scavenging for them whilst evading cannibalistic serial killers and saundering oil monsters invokes a sense of urgency that few games are capable of. 

The puzzles you face won't require much thinking, but might require some tinkering. They lack sophistication but manage to just be difficult enough to give the game a bit of a break up from the normal routine. 

The story is good and the universe will suck you in. Though, if you are a newcomer like myself, you will probably be a bit confused when characters or flavor items make references to things that you’ve never heard of before. 

Yet, it is not so disjointed that you will be unable to follow. It’s narrative is self-contained enough that you will invest in the characters despite all the missing pieces, and you will carry a sense of fear and curiosity with you as you explore the world. Despite not always understanding how things had happened, I never questioned why I was doing what I was doing or the urgency of my goals. I've seen many complaints about the ending, but it was satisfying enough for me. To be fair, I've come to understand that references made during the ending sequence were not all well received by series veterans, but as a newcomer, I did not recognize those references to find them frustrating. 

The graphics are good, but not great, and it takes some tweaking from the defaults to get anything close to what the trailers show off. As far as preformance goes, I had some stuttering between areas. Resident Evil 7 Is my second favourite survival horror game of all time right under Alien Isolation and it's also my second favourite Resident Evil game right after Resident Evil 4 (I never considered Re4 a survival horror game even though it's still my favourite game in the franchise). I think the game is well deserving to be called a masterpiece mainly because of how amazingly it takes the series into a new direction but still keeping the roots of the series. I feel like the people that are saying this is not a Resident Evil game are just judging it off the first few hours because nobody in their right mind would say that after experiencing the whole game. It really feels like classic resident evil in first person. You get some outlast, texas chainsaw massacre and some p.t vibes from those first few hours but later on it really becomes a traditional Resident Evil experience with the inventory management, the safe spots where you save the game and listen to the peaceful music, the infected creatures and crazy bosses, the weapons you acquire throughout the game, the environments, the atmosphere, the amazing intertwining level design where the whole map of the game connects together like the original mansion from the first game and different keys to unlock different doors as you progress and unlock more of the map. It's really the only Resident Evil game since the first where the title actually makes sense because there is evil inside a residence lol and it's another reason why it baffles me why some fanboys don't consider this a Resident Evil game.

 I'm getting pretty defensive about this game because I loved it so much. I think this is by far the best story and writing in the series, the story was never a strong aspect in the franchise but this game is the first one where I genuinely feel like it's a really great well told story. I liked the characters overall, I thought Mia in particularly was a very compelling and interesting character and I loved the villains in the game I thought the baker family were amazing. I loved exploring the whole game because the level design was so interesting. I think this is also by far the scariest game in the franchise, a lot of the scares worked really well and I thought the tension and suspense was really good especially when you're trying to get by a baker and some of the boss fights too. The game has some very creepy imagery and great memorable moments spread out throughout the game. Pretty much all of the horror aspects of the game is very well done and well-handled and it ends up being a great achievement that the developers were able to pull off especially after the action route the series went to. 

The shooting was really good too, I loved how the guns felt, handled and sounded. The variety in the weapons was good and the bullet impact on the enemies when you shot your weapon was well done too. As for negatives I think the game offered me a little too much ammo on normal difficulty especially towards the end but I know that’s not the case for everyone when I see some YouTube videos where the player is constantly running out of ammo. I kept saving up ammo for the grenade launcher for example thinking I would need it for later and once the credits rolled I noticed I never ended up even using it. I also don't think the game is as scary or suspenseful as Alien Isolation was mainly because there was barely any autosaving in Alien so there was a lot more suspense and tension because you didn't want to die and replay the game from where you last saved which could have been 10 minutes of gameplay but in Resident Evil 7 the auto saves are pretty frequent which takes away some of the suspense. The game is also more linear and scripted than Alien which I thought was ok because you do get a claustrophobic feeling sometimes and the scripted moments made the game feel more focused and memorable. 

None of the negatives I mentioned I thought took much from the game which is why I think it's a masterpiece and that is what a 10 means to me. Also the fact that I think the game is better than some other games that I consider a 10 and to be a masterpiece is the icing on the cake.

This was such a fantastic game to the franchise <(^_^)>. One of the best Resident Evils in many  years. When 7 was first announced back in the days I wasn't sure what to think about it after seeing the first trailer, as it was going to be in 1st person view. After trying the demo though on ps4 months ago, I felt that it was actually a really great way to do a new RE and to get out of that actionish style.

I've been a fan of RE since 1996, when I first played the original game with my brothers. For a 8 year old kid it was something incredible to play a bloody game of survival against zombies. Seeing how it changed into more action style during the years isn't what I wanted, but I still love RE4 and 5. 6th game was mostly an abomination (Leon's campaign was pretty good), I couldn't  get into Revelations games very well yet. 
So yeah, I've been hoping a long time for Capcom to go back to the more scary survival horror feeling, back to the roots. Because that is what I've loved RE for the most and they definitely managed to do it now. The horror is what RE is known for.

The story here is about Ethan Winters, who goes to search for his missing wife Mia. He happens to end up in a madhouse full of crazy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hillbillies. Enjoy the Baker family hospitality... I guess Ethan didn't play Silent Hill 2 or he might've known this is a bad idea to look for your wife.

Some might say that it is like Outlast or PT, but it's not. This game is clearly Resident Evil and you will notice it once you play further in the story. It's a good change to the gameplay, it adds new things but also don't forget the old fans like me. As it has things that are familiar from the PS1  games, that was nice to see. No kungfu moves (which is a good thing) like the action games have  with Michael Bay explosions everywhere.

Some seem to be complaining, that the game is too short which I don't really understand. Resident Evils often haven't been the longest games. Average completion time is about 10-15h maybe, depends how you play. Imo that is not too short. I personally love to play shorter games once in a while, because can't play games as much as before. Not every game need to be a Witcher 3 and horror games don't always work very well if they are too long. Many of my favorite games ever are less than 15h. RE7 took me 9h21min to complete on Normal difficulty which is a perfect length, but it felt a lot longer to be honest. 

Another complaint is that the game has 1st person. Well games have to change at some point and like RE changed with 4. So in a way it is better to try something new, instead of doing again what they did for many years. People often complain if things change and if they don't, can't satisfy everyone.

Capcom is back doing what they are best at. Resident Evils have been going on for 20 years and I'm glad they still know how to do it well, even if it's a bit different. The story is great, graphics are awesome, gameplay runs smoothly, no crashes, it has item customizations, it has puzzles, no coop and enjoyable boss battles. I'm not sure if I have the balls to try the Madhouse Mode difficulty yet >_<.

To me, it was scary and intense at many moments, and I've missed that feeling. I'm not gonna spoil the story or the ending, but just gonna say that the ending was cool ;). The story is different from the usual RE story. I do recommend this, especially to the fans of the games, but newcomers could enjoy it too if isn't too expensive. I loved pretty much everything about it. I also do often prefer 3rd person view, but the change works here and in my opinion, 1st person view brings the horror feeling better.

I just finished this MAGNIFICENT game and all I can say is wow! Capcom did one hell of a job at not only bringing Resident Evil back to it's horror roots, but also taking it to the next level! The story seems so original yet they still managed to tie it in seamlessly with the rest of the series. References to past events and returns of old names really brought a great sense of nastalgia to me! I've played RE & some of 2 and 3, still on my list of games to finish, but I became a lifelong fan after 4! Leon Kennedy was my dude! From all those games I played I'd have to say this one will remind you of the original! Residen Evil! Even though this game felt so new it felt so familiar and refreshing! 

So the story is great! I started out curious, then frantic and scared. The atmosphere really played a huge role in this too as everywhere you go you don't know if someone walking around abover is about to come attack you or if it was just one of the random sounds made throughout the Baker manor. At times when ammo wasn't scarce I found myself utter the phrase, "Cash me ouside!" then turning and running like a panzy when my clips where dry! As the stroy progressed it went from suspenseful to curiousity again and then it took a sorty melancholy turn. As the plot was further revieled I became somewhat empathetic to the Bakers & towards subject E-001. It was a nonstop roller coaster of events that "eventually" ends in classic RE style! "Use it!" ;) I say eventually because it did a great job of making me think it was "all over" and then bam! You get thrown right back into the game!

One thing Capcom really did well was making you choose what you wanted to take with you beyond the next save spot. With limited space for inventory you have to be VERY selective and tactful with what guns, ammo & health items you wanted to continue forward with. 

Lastly was the puzzles! Enough said. The shadow puzzles were unique and yet felt vaguely familiar! Broken shotgun. Collecting relics, misc. items & key cards to advance past certain areas really made this game feel like the originals. Also gather collectibles that are ramdomly placed througout the game was fun too! The parts where you watch video tapes to see past events and then re-enact them was very cool!

Overall I would say that if you have been a Resident Evil fan or a LONG time, or if you're just a fan of horror games in genereal & maybe RE never crossed your radar, you can definitely pick this game up and spend several (And I mean SEVERAL) hours exploring the Baker Estate & feel refreshed, nostalgic or immersed in this original yet classic-ish story!

Bout time they went back to the classic puzzle survival horror genre. Pretty awesome game, here's what I think is good and bad.

While playing the demo I was wondering how Capcom would make this game part of the RE lore. I was actually pleased to see a serious and dark tone, with more focus on the horror rather than that over the top action game that RE 6 is sadly known. At the sametime, however, I was afraid that the little cheesiness of the series would be lost, that maybe it would not have the b-movie tone expected from it. So I've been waiting for this game for months... Ever since I heard it was going to be a first person AAA horror game, I was VERY interested. In my rush to get the game pretty last minute (I don't know why I did), I decided to pay the extra $30 USD to get the deluxe edition because I really wanted the game. Anyway, point is, I ended up pre-ordering it. Now that the game is out, I have a few critiques about it, some good, some bad, and I have reached a final conclusion: It, was definitely worth the $90 I spent!

[h1]Good things about Resident Evil 7[/h1]
[list]
[*]First person - Finally! The game is in first person! I don't know, I think I'd prefer if it had choices between being first person, third person (like Resident Evil 4) and classic cameras.
[*]Optimized - The game runs amazing on my laptop! Even if I don't plug it in, and I don't lower the graphics it's still playable! So what I'm trying to say is, besides Resident Evil 1-3 (original versions of each), this is the first well optimized game for low end gaming...
[*]Atmosphere - The atmosphere is definitely required in any horror game, but this game exceeds in creating a good one. Every time I went around a corner, I felt dread thinking that [spoiler]Jack or Marguerite Baker[/spoiler] would find me. Except towards the end of the game, which I will get into later...
[*]Balanced Items - It's a really good thing in a game when you can carry 200 bullets in the magazine of a pistol that is fully automatic and fires .50 buckshot explosive shells, but in this game, you get just enough ammo, just enough power, and just enough accuracy to succeed, and nothing more.
[*]Puzzles - The puzzles are difficult, but not tedious. Sure, some of them are really hard, and I won't get into details as to what some of these are (simply because of the fact I don't want to spoil it since it's brand new), but some of them are recycled. One example of this is the [spoiler]shotgun[/spoiler] puzzle which was recycled from Resident Evil 1.
[*]Blocking/Dodging - Sure this could be labelled as "over powered" but trust me, in the [spoiler]chainsaw fight with Mia[/spoiler], it REALLY helps... Of course, in other points it's useful, but this is where it's most prominant...
[/list]
[h1]Neutral things about Resident Evil 7 (Good and bad)[/h1]
[list]
[*]Pre-order bonuses - So I'm sure it's known by now that the bonuses are as follows: 1 Strong First Aid Med, 1 First Aid Med, a few herbs and a defense coin, but these are a little useful to start the game with (especially the defense coin). But then, there's Madhouse difficulty... The creators even put a message in the game that recommends you not play it right off... It is cool, the fact that you have to ration Cassette tapes like old Resident Evil games (which is why when people say it's a throwback to the originals) is cool, but the difficulty itself is unforgiving... Have any of you actually played it? Let me rephrase this because I'm sure a lot of people did, have any of you made it past the first boss fight (or rather the first [spoiler]house[/spoiler])?
[/list]
[h1]Bad things about Resident Evil 7[/h1]
[list]
[*]Difficulties - So the game's been out for a while, everyone knows how the game plays (except people debating about buying the game and thus reading this), but everyone also knows how much of a difficulty swing there is from Normal difficulty to Madhouse difficulty. In Normal, it's kind of easy. I mean, it's still got a little challenge, but fairly forgiving. Madhouse difficulty on the other hand, is easily 3 times as hard. You have to be pretty perfect throughout the game. The first boss is ridiculously hard on this mode.
[*]Bosses - The bosses are hard in this game. They're more along the lines of Dead Rising rejects than Resident Evil bosses. I mean, they do change a bit and get cooler after each fight, but they're hard, and occasionally, forgetable. The bosses aren't just challenging, they're more along the tiers of, "If you don't do this right, and you don't concerve ammo, you will die!" I don't know why, they're just hard. Enough said really...
[/list]

In the end, I don't hate the game, but I say it could use some work. I still do love the game, and it's probably my new favorite game in the series... If you're debating about whether or not to buy it, just buy it.
