Of my thousands of hours of gamplay on steam this is my first review I've taken the time to write. 

Resident evil 7, I've waited a long time for this game, and was hoping for more. I beat the game at a casual pace in about 7 hours while attempting to collect as many extras as I could. I feel like that's a bit short, and adding a 2nd ending doesn't increase total game play much.

The entire time I was playing it I was wondering to myself, how does this tie into the franchise? Where's umbrella corp? T-virus? "insert letter"-virus?  Anything relating to resident evil aside from a mutated family and goop monsters. Well that itch was scratched (somewhat) within the last hour of game play, which still felt somewhat rushed. Up to then I was playing through confused as to why any of the game was taking place other than, your wife has been gone for 3 years and you recently got a video telling you she's alive, so as a good husband you go to rescue her. The game was still a fun play through though. 

They brought back storage crates for this just like in games before 4 with a limited backpack size. I don't mind this at all. It's mainly used to store extras and story items. I put some weapons in there and used them only once. I ended up playing through with a pistol and shotgun as my go to weapons. 

The final boss fight was rather disappointing. They're usually long action filled fights but in this game it felt more like a cut scene. Gun shots don't make a difference, you just shoot to progress the "cut scene" and then you're given an uber weapon that drops the boss in 4 shots, that's it, boss done. 

Overall it seems like they spent more time on graphics, audio/atmosphere, and vr for the game rather than lots of content and game play. They used a lot of cheap jump scare tactics to try and make it more "horror" but this seems catered toward vr players. Only a handful of times did they actually spook me with them. The atmospheric sounds weren't very scary, you could tell if they were gonna throw an enemy at you or not most of the time. So those sounds didn't add much "horror" effect in my experience (it's mainly just monster sounds and bumps and crashes in the walls and adjacent rooms. 

The "upgrade" system/antique coin system isn't an upgrade system and barely a cash system. In the entire game you can purchase a magnum (I purchased it and never used it) , health increase, or reload speed increase for yourself, not the actual weapons (like in other games in the franchise). 

Pros:
Beautiful graphics
Great atmosphere
Interesting character design (the family, not Mia or ethan) 
Interesting "world" you play in although it's rather small
Entertaining game play
Some adrenaline pumping moments 
Did I mention beautiful graphics? 

Neutral:
Unnecessary weapons (boss fights need to be tougher to really utilize the magnum and grenade launcher) 
Somewhat ties into the resident evil franchise because of bio-weapons
Enemies felt tougher than bosses (12 total deaths and only 2 from a boss) 
Catered toward vr play in my opinion 
Resources are scarce (ammo and health) since enemies don't have drops you must craft these items
Resources aren't so scarce once you realize psychostimulants show you where all the resources are that are tucked into nooks and crannies that you wouldn't normally check


Cons:
Short campaign 
Small world (only about 5 different areas on the property)
Not enough back story for characters 
Overall plot wasn't fleshed out enough (people just chase you screaming about family the whole game and the "why" is condensed and given to you toward the end of the game)

I was very apprehensive about the direction RE7 was going but I'm happy to say I was wrong and this game is fantastic. The biggest plus to the game is the tense atmosphere and the feeling of being a helpless baby while being chased around the game by people who just don't die.

The possitives are you have to make tactical decisions on if you want to fight or run, you need to manage your supplies and inventory, there are a lot of puzzles, there is a nice variety of locations, there is some backtracking but a lot is optional, the story has good pacing with a majority of it not revealed until the final part of the game (like all good horror films), the graphics are beautiful (I'm playing on 1080p max settings) and the characters are believable, you deffinately feel connected to the main character Ethan and want to help him to escape and find out what happened to Mia.

There are a couple of negatives but this feels like a little nit-picking. First would be there is a lack of diversity in the 'normal' enemies, they all look similar and while it's kind of explained later in my opinion it was just a convenient plot point to save on artist time. There are also some really easy to miss items, unlike older RE games there are no indicators (shiny stars) as to where items are, you can get medicine which shows you but it doesn't last long and you can end up wasting a lot of time hunting down an important item that's needed for progression.

The last thing I'd want to point out is to do with the season pass, thanks to Sony and Capcom's bone-headed exclusivity not only does the PS4 version get VR while PC and Xbox have to wait for a year, they also put a timed exclusive on the DLC, PS4 gets their first pieces on the 31st and some more two weeks later... on PC and Xbox we don't see anything until the 21st of Febuary. I'm very disappointed about this and would recommend not bothering to spend the extra for the season pass until mid-Febuary, at the moment it's just an extra £25 on the pricetag :\

This copy of the game was purchased via a third party site for 30 dollars. This review contains gameplay-related spoilers.

This has to be the most pathetic attempt at a classic Resident Evil I've ever seen. When it was first announced and revealed to have VR support, I feared that that aspect would heavily influence how the game played and my worries were not unfounded. The most obvious change was moving from a third person camera to first person but that's the least of this game's problems.

Do you remember the first Resident Evil? Whether it was the original or a remake, there was a brief cutscene at the beginning, but then after that you immediately started playing the game proper. In 7, you watch a brief cutscene, then you walk down a linear path for several minutes and find a VHS tape, which then leads to another sequence where you simply walk forward and wait for things to happen (there's even an invisible wall you run into if you don't wait for the game to tell you when it's okay to keep going). 

This whole tape sequence might as well have been a cutscene as the only point to viewing it is to see a character pull a switch needed to continue down the linear path. This was clearly meant to be an experience for the VR players but that means nothing to anyone who is playing the game normally (only the PS4 version has VR support). You then continue down the linear path and solve a "puzzle"(you unlock a door with an item that's in the same room) and then some more cutscenes happen and you continue to simply walk forward. Finally, after some more cutscenes and quick time events which are basically a tutorial for the combat, you get another major cutscene and then the damn game finally starts for real. This is after about 30 minutes of minimal interaction with the player. There are a total of 4 VHS tapes in the game that consist of:

1.	A walking simulator.
2.	A segment where you have no weapons and have to avoid an enemy while going down a linear path like SOMA or else it’s game over.
3.	A sequence that is entirely finding things to put in things.
4.	A sequence where you actually get to fight enemies and basically play like you do in the normal game(think of Ada’s sequences in RE2 except this one goes on for much too long).

Each of these tapes has you playing as a side character. The first three are skippable but contain information needed to get further through the game so they’re necessary evils during your first time. That info is not randomized however, so there’s zero reason to view the first three tapes after your first playthrough (you get an achievement for beating it in under 4 hours). I suppose this is a blessing as these were among my least favorites parts but it just feels like terrible game design.

After the dinner cutscene the game becomes noticeably less linear, but the classic RE game elements are barely there. Item boxes are present but you won't need them that often (there's an achievement for using them less than 4 times during the whole game). Ammo is initially scarce but becomes increasingly available to the point where it breaks the game (I had 6 weapons and almost 1000 units of ammo on me when I reached the final area and was mowing enemies down effortlessly). The iconic typewriters are nowhere to be found and the cassette players that replace them allow for unlimited saves. If that weren't enough, the game also automatically saves at numerous points outside the save rooms and even allows you to resume the game from them even if you quit out of it (As one user has commented, playing on Madhouse difficulty apparently removes the autosaves and forces you to collect cassette tapes for limited saves. That's a moot point howevever, as you have to beat the game once to unlock that difficulty. It'd be like having to beat RE3 on easy before unlocking hard). Like the old games, keys have to be found to further unlock certain rooms in an area and backtracking to previous areas occurs but less and less as the game goes on. The game also won’t throw the keys away for you once they’re useless like in classic RE games. That has to be done manually. Green herbs can be found and mixed with chemicals to strengthen their healing. Elements from the newer RE games include items that upgrade your maximum health and how quickly you can reload. These can be found or purchased with ancient coins you find laying around.


Puzzles in this game are practically non-existent. They almost entirely consist of finding a thing to put in a thing. And I’m not including keys. Some of them even have a child’s drawing or a note lying nearby that just straight up tells you the answer in case you were too stupid to figure it out on your own. Outside of those, the files in the game are mainly flavor text.
Combat in this game is laughable. You would think with a first person camera and precision aiming it would be more intricate like RE 4-6 but shooting enemies in the head or body is generally all that’s needed. While the designs for the molded aren’t the worst, they’re still rather bland and their 3 variants are the only regular enemies in the game aside from some mostly harmless bugs. The normal molded can easily be blocked and dispatched with a few bullets to the head or even the knife if necessary, the quick ones go down easily with any firepower you’ve acquired by the time you encounter them, and the fat ones are slow damage sponges that don’t appear often enough to even matter.

The Bakers are far less threatening than I was expecting. Jack only chases you around the house a couple of times and is easily eluded and can be put down with a few bullets to the head even if he corners you. His first boss battle is pretty basic and contains one of the stupidest sequences in Resident Evil history (and that’s saying something). Round 2, he takes only a little damage before starting up the second phase of the boss battle and the game then hands you a weapon with unlimited ammo that can be used for the remainder of it(cause that makes for a great challenge). His third and last boss encounter is arguably the best one in the game as it actually requires some fairly precise aiming and bears the closest resemblance to a classic RE boss fight(although even that ends with a scripted quick time event). Marguerite hangs out in a single room and is made trivial with a weapon you find in her area. After that you have another easy boss encounter with her and then one final battle in another area that is the only other boss fight in the game that isn’t piss easy.

The final boss (and I use that term very loosely) is a bigger slap to the face of RE fans than the entirety of Resident Evil 6. Since the game had given me so much ammo at this point, I was expecting it to be tough. Instead, I slowly walked forward while occasionally blocking its attacks until I got close enough to do a quick time event. After that, phase 2 started and I shot it handful of times which then triggered phase 3. Once again, I just shot it a few times and then another scripted sequence played out and some random guy hands me a pistol which I then used to shoot the final boss dead(remember that awesome part in the original Resident Evil where Brad Vickers tossed you a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ pistol to kill the tyrant? Me neither!).

I wish I was making this up. After all that item management and planning, I used up maybe a tenth of my ammo and killed the final boss effortlessly. Cut to a vague ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ending that’s basically Capcom saying, “Look! This game’s canon!”.

Capcom, please never make another Resident Evil game again. Remake 2 and 3 maybe (Or don’t. I don’t really give a ♥♥♥♥ anymore). Between Operation Raccoon City, 6, Umbrella Corps and this, I’m tired of seeing the series be sodomized.

This game actually has atmosphere and again a throwback to playing smart and micromanage your inventory etc. It also modernised the combat and put you in a first person view although it is by no means a first person shooter. 
It is very different from previous RE titles and at times it seems this horror game is about the supernatural instead of the biological explanations that has always been there in RE games. 

Personally I'd prefer this game to be a spinoff of the main franchise rather than a numbered game in the franchise because it does differ ALOT from both those expecting something like the good old days RE1-4 and Code Veronica, and from those expecitng an action game like RE5-6. And I think alot of the dissapointment from those givining it scores of 0 and 1 comes from just that, it beeing to different from those games. And the tieins to the RE world and old games are very minor to be even worth mentioning. 
It is very similar to other horror titles available though. Particularly on pc, cues from the style of Amnesia and Outlast are obvious, only with combat added. But make no mistake, on it's own it IS good. And had it not been a RE game alot of the same people trashing it now would score it alot higher.

Performance wise on my trusted soon 4yo rig, i7 4770K, 16GB RAM and GTX TITAN Black it ran at locked 60fps at maxed out 1080p. No drops whatsoever, no bugs and no crashes. I'd like a few more pc options but overall I'm very happy with the pc version of this game.

Finally a return to form for Resident Evil. This game recaptures the spirit of some of the older games with its gameplay cycle. You enter a room, prepared for the worst and most of the time you're ok to explore and find story related notes, or puzzle items, or combat items. And then you scour the next room. 

The combat is fine, it's a first person shooter. So it's not bad, it's just a bit meh, there's nothing really new or interesting to the combat that other games haven't done better. You're either kiting enemies or shooting their heads. It isn't particularly exciting by the end of the game, and the last hour is a typical end of game slog that feels like it drags on for a bit too long especially with some cheap monster spawn placements. There was one time I ran out of ammo for every weapon in the game, about midway through due to my own fault really, so I don't think there's much tension coming from scarcity. Rather it is the atmosphere and the sound design that keep you on your toes for the majority of the game. The game nails its atmosphere, the music is pretty awesome. Actually felt a little reminiscent to Diablo in save rooms. The boss fights are pretty exciting.

The puzzles seemed less like puzzles and more like get the 3 macguffins and put them in the magical locked door to proceed. There are a couple of puzzles, but they are very simple, you're more likely to forget you have a map and get lost then to be troubled by the puzzles.

The story is fine to good for Resident Evil. However the game seems to be missing a chunk towards the end, where an established character who you expected to encounter at some point seems to just disappear after threatening you. There also felt like a lack of video tapes. It seemed like there was room for more, and lots of places you could use them but there simply aren't many in the game. If you're completely unintiated and reading ♥♥♥♥♥♥ steam reviews for some reason, the videotapes in game are used to transport you to a past event where you will generally control a character exploring the locations in the game, giving you context or clues about what is going on or what might happen to you.

The game is incredibly short, I think I finished in roughly 7 hours. However, it's clear that the only way to add more length to the game would be to spend more time making quality scripted content, as attempts to artificially lengthen the game with combat would kill the game. I personally probably won't buy the DLC, but there is definitely potential for some cool stuff to be released if you're willing to pay again for more.

Good horror game, but definitely on the expensive side considering what you get for the money. I would recommend waiting for a sale unless you love heavily scripted horror games.

Here's what I think about the game in bulletpoints (and in poor english):

[h1]Negatives[/h1]
[list]
[*]The puzzles are stupidly simple. That's pretty much the only major flaw I see in this game. Remember the intricate "puzzle rooms" in older games? There's only one "puzzle room" like that in the entire game that I guess many people will solve with trial and error. Pretty much every other puzzle in the game is "use a thing on another thing, if that doesn't work try rotating the thing". Some of the puzzles will be immediately recognizable. Found a broken shotgun? If you've played RE1, you know what to do with it. I think they're trying to appeal to you with nostalgia, but that's just my guess.

[*]The game is short. Finished it in 8 hours on my first try. When you get to know the game, you can easily speedrun it under 4 hours (there's an achievement for that). The madhouse difficulty makes the game a bit more replayable. Fortunately more content is coming.

[*]Almost no connections to older games, storywise. Why is this game called Resident Evil 7 again?
[/list]

[h1]Positives[/h1]
[list]
[*]The game looks absolutely amazing. The PS4 version looks like crap compared to the PC version with everything on very high details. Wood really looks like wood, slimy things really look like slimy things. Plus the game is not really demanding, so you can enjoy really good looking graphics even with cheaper GPUs.

[*]The game is scary. I think. I've played so many horror games I'm not scared by them anymore. The game has a really thick atmosphere and many "uhh, I think I don't want to go down these stairs" moments.

[*]The story. Here's a mild spoiler: see that little person on the cover? Well, you can probably guess that little person is important. And you can also probably guess that it's a small child. Stuff like this has been done countless times in horror, especially games like FEAR. But, if you take your time and read all the logs, I'm sure you'll find the story interesting, mysterious and sad, in the classic Resident Evil sense (remember Lisa from RE1 remake?).

[*]Voice acting. And acting in general. Baker family is full of lunatics, and they act like it too. 

[*]Item management. Hey, standing next to an item box for five minutes, managing what you need is back! Being angry because you can't fit all your weapons into your inventory is back! Mixing things to get better things is back!

[*]Open world. Survival horror games are pretty much scary Metroidvania games with keys. Let me explain: when you get a new ability in Metroid, let's say double jump, you'll open your map and think: "Where can I use my new ability and what is the shortest way to get there?". It's pretty much the same in survival horror games, but instead of abilities you have keys. In RE7 there are moments when you'll get a key, you need to recall where you need to use it and you need to plan the shortest route. 

[*]Music plays when you're in a save room. I LOVE IT. 
[/list]

Overall, the game is pretty good and I recommend it, especially if you're a RE fan.

Intro: 
Resident Evil 7 is the return of the old school Resident Evil games that we know and love from the late 90's. This game is so good in fact that I was compelled to write a review for it, something I have done very few times. If you are looking for that experience that you had from Resident Evil 0, 1, 2, and 3 then this is definitely the game for you. Before writing this I beat the game on normal difficulty and want to play madhouse difficulty. I apologize in advance for comparing this game to the originals many times but honestly if you played the originals you will too.

Gameplay: 
Simply put, the gameplay is like Resident Evil 1 in first person. The game has an extremely low look sensitivity (at least default settings) that brings you back to the tank controls that were in the originals. The gunplay is fantastic and the weapons feel very real and powerful. Puzzles make a return, although not many of them are as difficult or complex as the games of old they are still enjoyable to try and accomplish. Boss battles are honestly few and far between but when you have them they are pretty great (I will not go into detail). The biggest thing that I love about this game is the first person POV. I can't stand how people are getting so mad about it being in first person. This has only made the experience better. Resident Evil 7 is truly survival HORROR because there will be times that I was just as scared as I was in Amnesia. Before this game I thought that if I had a gun there should be no fear, boy was I wrong.

Graphics: 
This game truly is beautiful and feels like the first real Resident Evil games due to the photo realistic style graphics. The game is pretty well optimized after I downloaded the newest nvidia drivers (a must have to play this game), my system is around 3 years old and I ran it on mostly highest settings with 50-80 fps. My suggestion is to turn off Shadow Cache and don't use HBAO+ for a much higher frame rate. Also use FXAA because for some reason FXAA + TAA would make the game really blurry, I don't know why. 

Story: 
This game is like any of the original Resident Evil games you play a character with little to no background, you get thrown into a crazy horror movie situation and you have to fight your way out. You play Ethan a man looking for his long lost wife who has been missing for 3 years. Ethan sets off to find her at the Baker estate and of course disasterous misfortune ensues.

Cons:
- No scary Resident Evil voice saying "Resident Evil 7 when I click New Game
- Occassional frame drops (could be due to my low end system in comparison to todays rigs however)
- Odd glitch where my monitor says no signal when changing graphical settings
- Needs more complex puzzles
- The community that is pissed over the fact it's in first person (what the heck guys it made the experience better)
- Compared to the original Resident Evil games it was quite a short playthrough time I beat it in 9 hours

Final Verdict: 9.5/10

Final Thoughts: 
This game should be the new path for the Survival Horror genre to go down. Like I said previously I have never felt so helpless and scared while carrying a weapon. Resident Evil 7 truly captured the feeling of being someone stuck in a truly horrifying experience with no training. One of the best parts of this game is that you aren't some soldier or cop like Chris Redfield and Leon Kennedy. You truly are the average joe stuck in a bad situation. This game is a must buy for any horror fan or Resident Evil fan.

Something awesome about the horror aspect of this game compared to something like Outlast (which is also a really fun horror game), is that you have quite a few weapons to defend yourself, unlike Outlast where you can only run or hide.  You know it's a scary game when you're walking down a hall with a 12 guage on your back, and a flamethrower in your hands, and you STILL manage to be scared every step of the way.

Ooooh, and the first person perspective!  I'll admit that when I saw that Resident Evil 7 was going to be a FPS, I was skeptical at how good it could be.  I saw some early gameplay and images and thought, "well that doesn't quite look like resident evil, but it doesn't look bad".  Honestly, it may not feel like Resident Evil for the first 30ish minutes, but that quickly changes somehow.  It just starts to feel familiar in some way which is just amazing.

Something else I have to praise the developers for is the wonderful optimization for the PC version.  It seems like every game that's made for multiple platforms just drops the ball for the PC version at launch *cough* Dishonored 2.  I'm 8 hours in and haven't run into any glitches, crashes, annoying bugs, or anything that took away from the experience.

10/10 I recommend this game completely.  You don't need prior knowledge of the previous games to know what's going on, but if you do know the Resident Evil lore, you'll appreciate some of the subtle references.  Whether you're new to the series, an old fan of the series, or just love the horror genre,  I suggest giving this game a play through.

Resident Evil franchise.... wow what a rollercoaster has it been. 1 through 3 and including everything in-between was slow-paced and more atmosphere focused than combat oriented, with static camera angles. the series was on a steady rise. Resident Evil 7 is a true revitalization of the franchise. That is strange considering it's the second time that's happened (See Resident Evil 4). A true return to form for the series, RE7 once again emphasizes horror over action. The atmosphere is unsetting, the imagry is horrifying and the story ain't half bad either. The gameplay is solid, you move slowly but not unreasonably so. Collecting and crafting items is rewarding and encourages backtracking, a staple of the series.The entire evironment is wonderfully put together and fun to explore. There are tons of secrets, puzzles and locked rooms that I couldn't wait to get into and solve. That said the puzzles are fun but quite simple, only one kinda stumped me but only for a few moments. The game doesn't really do complex or difficult puzzles. The Boss fights are fun, though I'm not so sure they were really needed. Especially since you fight one boss 3 times. You also have to play hide and seek with that boss throughout that segment (Same with another) and that kinda felt unnessiary as well. Each fight is distinct, especially the last, but it felt like if one of those encounters were cut not much would be lost. The Graphics are stunning to look at and for the most part the game runs remarkably well. I did, however, run into a bit of framerate stuttering or straight up momentary freezing (using an i7 and 1060 6GB so there is no way it's my hardware). On top of that some facial animations just didn't trigger leaving a blank face on an NPC talking (probably scarier than whatever was supposed to be there) and a cutscene stopped and then moved onto the next. These are all rare and minor problems sure to be patched out, however. Overall Resident Evil 7 is a great horror game and a breath of fresh air in a franchise that had lost it's identity. Because that is what the game really get's right. It's identity. Resident Evil 7 is the first game in a long time to truly feel like Resident Evil. It has recaptured the magic that made me, and many others, fall in love with the series in the first place. If you're a fan of the series or just want a fun horror game to play this is defintiely worth your time. I cannot recommend it enough.

The game starts off in a way that some people will have the "this is not resident evil feeling" but you  once you get passed the first hour, which is basically a story set up for the rest fo the game, you will feel the old resident evil games. Lock picks, different animal keys that make you go back to old locations, finding ammo and herbs, the save points, item boxes, they are all there. With addition to, there are the bobble heads and the antique coin system. Bobble heads are destructable collectables  where you have to knife them ot shoot them (listen for them), the antique coins you will find their use later where the bobble heads i missed 3 of them which im assuming is for an achievement other than that idk their purpose. You also can craft ammo, health and stronger versions with items in game. 

The first person element just works. I was skeptical at first but it really does work well. I would reccoemend if playing with a controller, the sensitivity starts at a "4" by default. I chose to raise it to "10" the max bc it would take you a long time to turn around and is very very slow. HOWEVER there is a feature that the game did not tell me until half way through that if you hit left stick down and "B" at the same time you will quick 180, like in older games. It really also makes the game more thrilling, youll find yourself constantly turning around to see whats there due to the ambient noises and being "trained to be worried". JUST TO PINT OUT, people ask is it scary is it scary or just cheap pop ups? Its scary most of the time id say depending on your definition of scary and the pop ups are unexpected and not cheap or annoying. They fit really well, arent over or under used and you will forget they happen until they do.

As far as the game looks, ill put this out right now. At first you wont be impressed and you wont be. Also there was a lot of jagged edges no matter what aa i used. Some settings cause wierd shines , and other settings cause fps drops like  shadow cache and very high shadow quality settings. When the game starts getting a little stale toward the final 3rd it manages to fix it by changes up a bit. Cant go into farther detail but it does well. 

To note there is maybe 5 different enemies in the game, 3 of them are variations of one enemy.

The sound is really where the game shines, you hear something and wonder, you will be afraid to go down certain cooridors, you will get nervous. Im not one to ever feel anxious in scary games and movies but it got me.

Resident Evil is a return to form for the long running series. Which Capcom has successfully returned to its survival horror roots. That atmosphere is particularly eery thanks to the excellent sound design. From the sound of footsteps on the floor above, to the sound shutters banging against the house due to wind. You really feel as if you're trapped in a delapidated and depressing home fighting for your life. This all is helped by the series first foray into being completely played in first person. Whether it's hiding from an stalking enemy or slowly opening a closed door, the tension is definitely ramped up thanks to this change. It's something I was nervous going into the game, but it feels right at home as you progress. 

There are a multitude of puzzles that harken back to the orignal games. Puzzles initially start out as simple "Bring item A here" soon become more involved and intricate, which due to potential spoilers I won't go into detail. Tense enemy encounters with eery environments really trigger memories of nostalgia for past games. Gone are the stylistic action set pieces that series previously diverged into. RE7 returns to the frantic feeling of you versus an imposing foe with limited resources. Every decision matters and a bad one could be your last.

I say this with no small amount of emotion, having played Resident Evil since the first and having followed the universe through every stage of my life: This game is amazing. 

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Short review: This game is creepy, but still maintains the elements that made the earlier Resident Evils so amazing-- You can fight, run or hide but your only salvation will be through the sheer willpower to see yourself out of the nightmare you're in.. and until you can do so, expect a scare around every corner and a certain faith put into your shotgun.

To list some negatives, the game seems to have a downward spiral of intrigue. You'll reach a point in the game where you get more questions than answers and a hopelessness for having them, well, answered. The game continues to get more and more detached from reality as you go, which-- in my opinion-- detaches you from the action and thus makes the experience less scary. That's not to say that the mystery isn't still mysterious, and that the game doesn't still make you think twice before entering that dark hallway..

9/10

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Long review: I've been playing the Resident Evil 7: Beginning Hour demo/teaser since it was released. I saw all the updates to it and made it a twisted parlour trick to show people how much I knew about the demo-- dirty coin, murders, etc-- but admittedly I was apprehensive of the main game before it came out. I was aware of just how bad a developer could screw up a game despite it's fantastic appearance in the demo and teasers, and had absolutely no faith in the brand at this point. To me, Resident Evil had become synonymous with cheap scares, campy dialogue and over-the-top action ever since it became more of a movie than it was a game and we saw such installments as Operation Raccoon City and RE5/6

When I first started the game, I was delighted to see the game was still very similar to the demo in all the right ways. Controls, cinematics, cutscenes, all that good stuff-- the game pulled me in quite readily and made me and everyone who was with me at the time jump at every corner before we really got INTO the main game. 

To give away some of the game's elements without spoiling it's content: The game features a series of "areas" and a variety of bosses, each having throwback themes to bosses from previous Resident Evil games. You'll see a healthy and familiar amount of "infection" in old, disgusting RE manner, and while you're trying to get through the scariest tight corners and closed rooms that you can, you'll find that the game rewards a certain bravery by placing hidden items all over. The creators of this game were clearly familiar with how it felt to have only 2 rounds in your shotgun before entering a dank basement, and then finding 6 more in a lockbox nearby.

There are secrets-- not quite as tedious or hidden as in the Demo, thank god, but still secrets all the same. If I had to liken this game to another, I would say it feels almost like Amnesia with it's slow, dark corridors and sense of dread, but to tell you the truth I cannot compare this game to anything but Resident Evil. You're scared, but not helpless. You're trapped, but not stuck. The game encourages the player to be as brave as they want to be, whether you're like me and you choose to sink all your ammo into the eldritch horrors that shamble towards you in order to stop them even if for a moment, or more-like a friend of mine who chooses to crouch-walk away from everything that goes bump in the night. These options will severely impact the way you play the game and the way the game plays you.

The negative side of this game comes later. The game becomes increasingly labyrinthian (not literally-- I mean it becomes more and more mysterious, presenting plot-twists without ever really explaining them) and at a certain point, I *personally* found myself becoming disillusioned with the plot and wondering when it would end. *NOT* because the game had become boring, but because the thing that drove me to giddily check every terrifying room of the house had suddenly lost it's allure. It's almost as if I had accepted that there were powers at play in-the-game that I had no business in really investigating. Some things were inexplainable and as-such felt like a waste of time to search for answers-for, but these things began to blend in with the plot that *needed* answers in order to progress, so I couldn't differentiate between the unknown and the soon-to-be-known fast enough.

Another negative side is the characters. NOT The enemies you encounter, as I'm as-delighted with them as I've ever been, but rather the two female companions you have in the game. Mia and Zoe (no spoilers) are uninteresting at best. They ♥♥♥♥♥ at you, they complain as if they're the ones trudging through gore and horror to get to them, and there's very little reward to finally finding them after all those hours. I can POSITIVELY say that the main character-- Ethan-- is very relatable. You'll find yourself going "Oh ♥♥♥♥, what the ♥♥♥♥?" just as he does so in-game. In the lore, his behavior doesn't make much sense (A bystander to all these horrifying events would probably just break down, have a panic-attack and die) but the player can relate to him in-that he sees something awful, addresses it with confusion or terror, then quickly confronts it head-on, and finally taunts it with a cocky retort when it's been bested-- just as the player might in their head. It's better to see him as an extension of yourself than he is an in-game character, which can simultaneously help and hurt the immersion.

Contrary to what alot of people think, the game has INCREDIBLE replayability. The first time you play it will be to figure out the plot, to encounter the horror, and the second-- while the horror and jumpscares may have worn off-- can be to master the game. To expend less ammo, to solve the puzzles faster, to find the secrets that you wish you had in the first playthrough. I recommend it.

There's also several VERY CREATIVE elements of the game that left me and my real-life companions in shock. Enemies will behave in unique ways to different actions, wounds (either to yourself or to enemies) will prompt unique and ever-changing reactions, and you will find a plethora of weapons that change the way you face the seemingly-once-unstoppable adversaries, and in-turn, the way that THEY face YOU. The AI of this game is smart when it's working correctly, though, admittedly, it has it's faults (Such as one time where a shambling beast turned and hugged a wall instead of following me, and did so for so long that I found I could reload all my guns whilst waiting for it to correct.)

In summation, this is an amazing game and I am JOYOUS to have been proven wrong in my fear of it's success. This is one of the only games I've ever bought for full-price, on release day, and haven't regretted. If the creators can keep this up, keep the game fresh. Even if not-everyone purchases this game, I firmly believe everyone should see it and be familiar with it, because-- varying on how the creators proceed from here-- you may be looking at the REVIVAL OF RESIDENT EVIL!

Resident Evil 7 was a game I was highly anticipating after it was announced. All the people fighting over if it's Resident Evil or not, if it's gonna be good or not, didn't stop me for being incredibly excited for this game and this game lives up to my expectations and even surpasses them.

The Story:

Resident Evil 7 puts you in the shoes of Ethan. After his wife Mia disappears for almost three years he get's a disturbing message from her which contains a tearful goodbye. Wanting to find out what happened to his wife Ethan travels to Dulvey, Louisiana. Once there Ethan enters a seemingly abandoned house, but after some time he finds that the house is not abandoned and in fact is inhabited by the Bakers, a family of three, Jack, Lucas and Marguerite and Ethan is put in a fight for his life as he tries to save Mia and leave the Baker Residence. 

The story in itself is rather intriguing as it has a very mysterious feel to it. You don't know much about anything as the game doesn't flat out tell you the story. Most of it is told through paper clippings, photos, journals and VHS tapes which you can watch to find out what other souls went through when they wound up in the Baker residence. I found the story incredibly captivating which pushed me to keep playing until I figured out everything.

The voice acting for the characters I felt was alright. I liked Jack, Mia, Marguerite and Ethan, but the voice actor for Lucas truly over did it. Some of the lines he delivers are too over the top.

Gameplay:

Most fans have been annoyed by the fact that Resident Evil 7 was first person only, but to be honest ? This helps out the game to be even more scarier. The limited vision once you travel through the halls of the house and hear noises coming from seemingly every direction helps build tension which would have never been able to achieve with third person. But for those stating that this is not Resident Evil, it's more Resident Evil than the last 5 games in the series.

The most memorable stuff from previous RE games make a comeback in this game. Inventory management, safe rooms, limited resources. Even the puzzles are very RE like. Some of the puzzles include looking for pieces of a sculpture to open a door, which is very nice nod to previous games. 

The combat in this game is a bit different from the stuff you have seen in the previous RE games. Ammo and in general all resources are incredibly limited, so you must save your ammo and use it wisely and make every single shot count. The game gives you Pistols, Shotguns, SMG, Flamethrowers and Grenade Launchers to sink your teeth in, but again ammo for these guns are incredibly limited, so you'll mostly use Pistols and Shotguns.

Most of the fights tend to get incredibly violent and the game in general is incredibly violent. Probably even more violent than the other titles in the Resident Evil franchise.

Now for the enemies. Once the game starts, you're gonna be hunted by the Baker family. Unlike other enemies you can't kill Jack or Marguerite. They are faster and stronger than you so it's best you are not seen by them. But if you are spotted your options are to run away and hide or you can waste your ammo and stun them. They will go down, but will get back up again and will hunt you down. The only other type of enemies you see are the Molded, which are these black gooey monsters which are usually in groups, but fighting them is usually simple as a few well placed headshots will take them out.

Boss fight also make a return and the boss fights in this game are absolutely amazing. Intense would be an incredible understatement. Some of my favorite moments are the boss encounters in this game.

Graphics and Audio:

Graphically the game looks absolutely outstanding. The environments look incredibly and all of them are incredibly detailed. The game looks the best once the setting is night as some of the day textures are a bit mediocre. 

Audio design is absolutely phenomenal. Playing this game with a good pair of headphones is a must. Once the game starts and all the surrounding sounds kick in you are immersed in this world and in the later segments the audio design is phenomenal. When you wander through the houses and hear creeks, weird noises and the bakers shouting while they're stomping around looking for you make for an incredibly intense game.

Problems:

This game does suffer from some very minor issues which I will not deduct points for as I think these are just minor nitpicks of mine.

The game had one bug which I only encountered at one section of the game. I got stuck in a railing and I had to force shutdown the game to fix it. Until the end of the game it's the only bug I encountered.

The puzzles are all incredibly simple. It's usually pick something up and bring it to a specific location and that's basically it. I think more depth for the puzzles would have been nice, like the Happy Birthday puzzle. 

Length:

The game took me 8 hours to finish, but this game has tons of replay value. This game has two endings, the madhouse difficulty which gives you limited saves and resources are even more scarce and not to mention collectibles and stuff like that, so more or less you are looking at a 20+ hour game.

Closing remarks:

Resident Evil 7 is return to form. It's scary, intense, incredibly fun and all around an excellent game. Resident Evil 5 and 6 sold incredibly well and Capcom could have just made 7 into another action fest, but they took care and brought the series back to it's roots and the succeed in making one hell of a game. If you like Horror games this is a must, if you like Resident Evil this is a must, hell this is a must play in general. I would honestly say it's worth to get it as soon as possible.

Final Rating:
9.5/10

Well I'll try to keep it brief here and avoid spoilers.  

After seeing through the demo footage of the long-aviated seventh iteration of the Resident Evil franchise I could barely hold my excitement.  Abandonment of the action-packed running-&-gunning traditions of the previous 2 games ( even though 4 is generally regarded as the one setting the tone for the last 3, it is still considered one of the best RE games by  many fans)  and return to series' horror roots, what else could a fan like me crave from next Resident Evil game ? And indeed, the game delivers intimate horror with a tightly focused scope and all the trappings you'd expect from a survival game. 

However, things start to deteriorate much faster than you could have expected as both narrative and gameplay run short of the abovementioned traits less than halfway through the campaign. First 5-6 hours are brilliant to say the least and fully reflect both the opening hour demo and early gameplay footages, but after completing the first chapter and basically, the only expansive area of the game, everything just turns into completely mediocre corridor action, with no tension of suspense whatsoever. What’s happenin’ Capcom? The first chapter proves you have full understanding of how fans wanted to see series’ reboot. What got all your enthusiasm wiped out so fast remains a mystery to me.

Another thing putting me completely out of temper is the actual length of the game. Is very short. It took my around 11 hours to complete the campaign, which is nothing by RE standards. Moreover, the boss encounters are rare with half of the fights being more annoying than intense. While the total mediocrity of the campaign, especially its 2nd an 3rd chapters, should have been enough to give it an average rating of 6/10 , I would still give it 7/10 for brilliant opening, tense atmosphere of the first campaign and unprecedented amount of visual detail.  What could have become one of the best RE games in the serious is un unfortunate example of yet another cashgrab profiting from the feelings of devoted fans. What a shame (( . 

I would like to add that I am not trying to dissuade any of  RE fans from buying this game. Try it and make your own conclusions.

I'll admit it, RE7 is a huge gimmick of a game. A joke. The game was meant mostly for VR. This game shows what's wrong with a lot of new games these days. The whole game is filled with predictable scripted events. It has a creepy atmosphere, but most of the scares are cheap thrills through the use of scripted events rather than trying to build up an atmosphere full of tension. The atmosphere stays exactly the same from beginning to end. It is creepy at first, but it doesn't hold up and it soon gets old and tiresome. When the game is "quiet", it requires a lot of patience to slowly walk or "jog" (if you can even call it that) from one linear hallway, to the next. This gets worse when you have to backtrack to solve "puzzles". The game rarely ever puts you into a wide open area. It follows a strict path of left to right or right to left with maybe a few doors along the hallway to check out. There are guns. I don't know why but there guns and I sware the gunplay seems to also be scripted as well. When you shoot the main character enemies, it is scripted when the enemy either "dies" or falls to the floor. It feels like there is no freedom in the game, even when exploring ( what little there is to explore). Whether you walk 2 feet, 3 feet, 7 feet, into a new area it's another scripted event after another. Should I have typed, "spoiler alert"? Replay value for this game is ZERO. Absolutely none. It plays exactly the same the second time as it did for the first. It's only an 8 hour game full of  movie-like events that come and go the same way no matter how many times you play it. There is almost no reason to "outsmart" the enemy as they are not smart to begin with (and they are scripted anyway, so most of the game just plays itsself when fighting enemies). The only part you have to think about are the so called "puzzles" which take literally only 15 seconds to solve. 

The inventory system is also a joke. Similar to Deadspace, there are safe rooms with a save spot and storage boxes where you can place and infinite amount items from your over loaded inventory, annoyingly, placed in the most convient of places. This causes some issues with the "survival feel" of the game. Too few were the times where I had to really think about the consequences of using or giving up certain items in place of items more important. After playing this game once, I have no incentive or desire to want to go back and play it again. This game just a gimmicky, big budget VR walking simulator, but with a creepy atmosphere. VR really hurt this game and it is obvious when you look at the slow movement of the character (even when jogging to prevent motion sickness), the way the weapons are held, and the "in your face" jump scares. Every jump scare is meant to be viewed through the headset.

 It is a 460 dollar game meant to be combined with a VR Headset. With no replay value, it is meant for a one time gimmicky playthrough of 8 hours. 

I would only reccommend this game to those that are twitch or youtube streamers who want to get easy followers and subscribers streaming this game through a "scare cam". (Is that what people call it these days?)

They did it boys and girls. They brought Resident Evil back.

 (Keep in mind that this review is coming from someone who didn't particularly enjoy RE5 and disliked RE6 heavily.)

 Don't let the change from third-person, or the VR demo fool you, in no way does this game attempt to jump on the P.T. bandwagon in a misguided attempt at cash-grab. It chooses instead to completely harken back to the classic RE experience—and manages to do so superbly.

 Ammo is scarce, enemies are dangerous and the dialogue charming and sometimes straight-up goofy (somewhat reminiscent of RE1). The shift in perspective from third, to first-person together with stiff movement manages to perfectly recreate the feel and effect of the old and busted tank controls, without actually making it feel just that. Having to turn away and run from enemies to regain distance, thus forcing you to let them out of your field-of-view is an excellent way to instill fear and panic in the player, something only possible (to this degree at least) in an FPS. 

 The enemies not being able to go through closed doors—albeit feeling somewhat arcade-y—also strengthen the nostalgia factor. Bosses are fun and intense, weapons feel good and the story is pretty decent for RE standards. NG+ and certain achievements offers fancy unlockables, making a second, third and forth play-through both fun and rewarding.

 By beating the game (if you didn't per-order it) you get access to the “Madhouse” difficulty, the one I did my first play-through on. Not only do we get the good old ink ribbons (this time as cassette tapes) back, but item placement is completely different. Ammo is as rare as gold and enemies don't ♥♥♥♥ about. This is the difficulty I feel best compliments the game, and is thus wholeheartedly recommended for anyone looking for that extra challenge.

 Be warned though, the game is short. I completed my first run in slightly under 7 hours, and that is with me taking my sweet time doing so. Although my actual playtime is probably closer to 10 or 11 hours with all the game overs and what not. With that being said, I do feel like NG+ do offer some extra value to that money, but if that is not your jam I would suggest waiting for a price drop.

 The biggest negative I can currently come up with is that the game is a bit too heavily scripted. Cut-scenes and cinematic events are certainly abundant, and although I actually didn't mind them at all whilst playing, I feel like they might hamper the enjoyment during a 2nd play-through. Also, enemy variety is not as good as in recent installments. Even though it wouldn't really be justifiable within the current story to have more enemy types, I feel like they could've been a bit more creative.

 At the end of the day, I feel like Resident Evil 7 is a love letter to the franchise's fans. If you have played any of the first games in the series the game will immediately feel familiar and homely. If I had to give my opinion right this moment (after having just completed the game) I'd say this is easily one of the better games in the franchise. Although, I might be somewhat biased ATM, seeing as how the game ends with a 100% throwback to the original, as well as a familiar face. (And the promise of upcoming free content.)

 Anyways, since I lack imagination, I'll simply end the review with a TLDR. Thanks for reading.

 TLDR; I strongly recommended this game for fans and newcomers both. It manages to recreates the feel of the original splendidly, whilst modernizing just the right places. Combat is tense, story above average and the dialogue charming. The game is short (around 5-10 hours) but makes up for it in replayability. The heavily scripted sequences might get annoying during replays. Madhouse is the way to play.

This is a game so good, it prompted me to actually write a review IMMEDIATELY after playing.
After having put a few hours into this game over several days, I can say this game is a blast, start to finish.

The atmosphere and graphics are head and shoulders above anything else on the market in the past 2-3 years. The sparse lighting and narrow corridors fill you with dread, knowing you have very little room for error, and the game handles it's graphics BEAUTIFULLY. An old, rotting house never looked so good.
And if you're worried about the game capturing the feel of the earlier ones, have NO fear: This game does  a great job recreating the kind of gameplay that the first three games were all about. If you liked the limited ammo, inventory management, and tough enemies of old, this new one will not disappoint. It even takes place in a mansion just like 1, and has a reference or two to the others as well! 

The story will be a point of contention for some people. And no, you won't see many of the old characters from the other games. You'll hardly notice, though, and the Molders replacing zombies and the Baker family as bosses do an excellent job filling the shoes of their ancestors. It's a gripping story, as you really do want to know more about the Bakers, and find out just what the heck happened to make them this way. It's nothing mind-blowing, but it will satisfy and wrap-up nicely by the end.

Buyers beware, though: It's not a perfect product. At times,  the second half of the story felt a lot more action-oriented and it DOES lose that horror sheen towards the end.  It'd be nice if they could have kept that going through the whole game. 
Also, if you have an AMD card or an ultrawide monitor, you might not want to get this game. 21:9 is not supported, and AMD cards are having issues at the moment. Consider waiting for a patch if you have either.

Otherwise, this is the return to roots Resident Evil NEEDED. Recommended to almost anyone that likes horror games or Resident Evil.

Alright, this is my first ever Steam review but I'll do my best. Be warned though, this will be relatively long.

I went into this game not knowing much about it, I had played the demo and seen a few of the trailers but other than knowing it was a PT-esque horror game I didn't know anything about it, and oh boy was I in for a surprise. First of all I will start off by saying that this [i] is [/i] a horror game but it also has a story - and a decent one at that.

[h1] PROS [/h1]

For starters visually the game looks great; most textures and character models look fantastic and the lighting in the game is very well done. What stands out as the best thing in the game though is the horror and tension, this game is listed as a horror game and it certainly lives up to that. The atmosphere in this game is fantastic and the tension it builds is insane. The best thing is that it's not just all jumpscares either, I can only think of around four or five jumpscares that occur in the entire game. Most of the horror is created through atmosphere, tension and the fear of not knowing what lies ahead or behind a door, which doesn't sound that great but it's executed brilliantly. The audio in the game really adds to the world building and overall is very good, it also gives you some much needed insight into what unseen things are happening around you. The world is very well done and the way it is laid out allows you to revist most areas so you don't have to worry about not being able to explore areas you missed or not being able to recover things that you left behind. The story is also surprisingly good, it has a few twists and turns and I never found myself getting bored. As you can see I have 19 hours on record for this game and that is due to the fact that I restarted at one point just so I could re-live the first part of the game which is [i] absolutely amazing. [/i] The gameplay and combat in the game is decent and there may be a few parts where you actually find yourself being challenged.

[h1] CONS [/h1]

To be honest there aren't many cons I can think of for this game, I guess some things that people may not like are the difficulty of some boss battles or the number in which some enemies show up but overall everything is pretty darn good. There are a few moments where you may find yourself a little stuck as what you're supposed to do next but with a little thought and exploring you should be back on track in no time. If anything I'd say the biggest con is that the first half of the game is reasonably better than the second. There comes a point where the horror starts to disappear a little which takes away some of the appeal but it's nowhere near enough to ruin the game or make you lose interest.

[h1] CONCLUSION [/h1]

Overall I would have to say Resident Evil VII is a fantastic game, I thoroughly enjoyed my time playing it and would have to say it is probably the best horror game I have played so far. There were countless moments in the game that really left me shocked and absolutely amazed at what was going on - some absolutely insane things happen in this game. If you're looking for a horror game that will put you on the edge and give you a bit of a challenge then I would most certainly recommend it, but I would also definitely recommend it to anyone who is looking for a very well executed first-person horror game.

On a final note because I know a few of you will be asking this; it took me just over eight hours to complete this game on normal difficulty and I'm one of those players who takes his time to really explore everything. Not the longest game but I think for what it is it's the perfect length.

[h1] 8/10 [/h1]

It took me 8h30 to finish the game for the first time in Normal mode, which is the normal amount of time required for a Classic Resident Evil (before RE4).

Resident Evil 7 feels like you're playing RE1 again but in first person mode. You'll have a lot of easter eggs from the old trilogies (the sounds from RE3 while you type on a certain digicode haha.), but with a pretty good atmosphere that will remind you of Texas Chainsaw and Evil Dead, while maintaining a biohazard tone.

Typically, it's the real and only Resident Evil you need if you hated Resident Evil 6. Everything is in it :

-Manual saves (unlimited and there are checkpoints in normal mode, fewers checkpoints and limited amount of saves in Madhouse Mode)
-Interconnected Chests ! YES.
-Limited inventory, although you'll find some bags to extend it further into the game.
-Limited ammo and healing items: Be sure to think about the best decision you'll have to make. Do you wanna kill everything or flee ? Best thing is to keep ammo. Normal mode is not that hard though.
-Magnificient sound/level design: Virtual 7.1 Surround works like a charm, you'll know exactly where sounds are coming from and general quality for the sound design is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good. Voice acting is totally cool, especially for Jack. Going through the Baker's property is totally incredible. Level Design is very good and general progression makes you feel like you don't even want to put the controller down. This is Classic RE: You'll need a specific item/key to progress into rooms you couldn't before etc.
-Length is good enough; You can beat the game between 6 to 10 hours I guess, maybe more if you're really struggling. Aknowledge the fact that this was my first playthrough in NORMAL mode. It will be different in Madhouse Mode.

[ A fact about Madhouse Mode: Madhouse is the hard difficulty for this game and it feels even more like Classic RE. Items aren't at the same place than normal mode, enemies are more aggressive and faster, and you'll need to find cassettes to save your progression (although, as I said before, there are still some checkpoints but not as many as normal mode). Cassettes are typically the same kind of item than Ink Ribbons. ]

-Story is good enough to keep you entertained, although the last hour was kinda like a typical "oh ♥♥♥♥, we need some action parts here!" from Capcom. It's not "Action Resident Evil 5/6" though, but still a bit more "pew pew" than the rest of the game. 
-Bossfights: Some people will find them pretty meh, I find them to be totally correct, especially when you know that if you do 1 thing, boss will do this thing, etcetera. In fact, there are some events that you'll see only if you do a certain thing while in the bossfight, making it pretty interesting.


Guys, I know this game won't be for everyone, especially people who loved Resi6. It's like a love letter from Capcom to old fans, while keeping the game fresh. First person view was, at least to me, a good choice for Resident Evil since I don't think fixed camera will still work on us now. This game has a good progression, story, sound/music, some memorable characters, a good gameplay. What more do you need ?

Resident EVIIL (7) is probably the most hands on in touch release in the series since 4. All the hype was worth it, though i'm not an advocate of hype in general.

Story: 9/10
Great pacing, no shortage of things to do and no long endless droning on in general. Well played and properly told. Overall a tremendously well done job given this one had a lot riding on it. Minor gripe (though minimal) is that the real story only really gets going partly halfway through.

Sound / Ambiance: 9/10.
It's scary at the right times, builds up proper tension and is doing this whole "jump scare" thing very well. Not overdone, not underdone, just right in my opinion. Atmosphere works fantastically and dynamic sound and general effects are fantastically done.

Gameplay: 10/10.
I'm a firm believer like most of you out there that the series went catastrophically downhill since 4. This one really takes it back up to a respectable standard, keeping that literal 1-3 feel without sacrificing going into a new direction regarding perspective and general gameplay mechanics. Everything in this fits very well together and doesn't make it feel like they just copypasted outlast or similar titles. Yes, there's a lot of influence but in the good way.

Longevity: 8/10.
Yes, there's unlocks. Yes, there's replay value. The game runs a semi RNG algorithm that mixes up certain elements of the playthrough in general, and there's the good old weapon unlocks as in older series. This counts heavily since there are also multiple endings and cross sections in some parts of the game. The length in general is fine. i've completed this with roughly 80%^ discovered in 10h48m and took a slow approach. The only slight issue i have is that the DLC is clearly not going to add to the main game in a huge way, which is a bummer. Also some of the more key aspects of the game were rather well overlooked, but not a giant hindrance.

As some users have vocally thrown up all over the steam discussion forums, there are some issues with the pc release but i've experienced little to none of those. *DISCLAIMER* if they had, my review would not be altered in any way. (AKA learn to set up your rig properly before complaining the game is crap)

Overall: 8.5/10. A solid entry in a long standing franchise, which for the first time in a long time brings hope and joy, and not "oh look its another one".

Resident Evil 7 is, by all accounts, very much a classic RE game caught in some weird modern-survival horror twist. The first hour or so, depending on how much you can handle and how quick you explore, is very much akin to the likes of recent horror games. Stealth is key, and your resources are low enough to not justify using them so quickly. Its tense, and geniunely scary in a way you've experienced before. Then, it blends seemlessly into that classic RE feel. Examining items, inventory managment, limited ammo and an abundence of enemies that, while stronger than you, are able to be taken out if you've got the skill for it. You'll feel right at home with how the gameplay loop works itself out, if you've ever played the first few REs. And this isn't just rose-tinted glasses speaking. "Oh, its good because it feels like old RE". It just WORKS. Who knew, in 2017, that the formula for RE1-3 would hold up? It's crazy. There's just this real sense of progression and discovery with each new area you explore... This revitalization of a bloated and confused series is exactly what it needed; to jolt some energy back into its corpse and allow it to breathe again.

For a long time fan, this is honestly exciting. If you HAVEN'T played any of the older Resident Evils, or even any Resident Evil in general, I suggest picking this game up. While canonically it takes place after RE6, the world Capcom setup feels just as disconnected and bubbled as Resident Evil 4. The audio is ambient as hell. The old house creaks and croaks as you explore for puzzles pieces and resources. The dialogue is written well, and there are rarely any facepalm moments(depending on how you feel about the tone of the game). Gunplay feels and plays firm. Guns echo powerful blasts as they're fired and the enemies react accordingly, whether you shoot them in the head or the leg, damage will show up as they are hit and they stumble back in the most responsive way. And the replayability is THERE, for sure. It's probably not as replayable as say, RE4 or 5, but there are secrets to unlock, and difficulty effects the general layout of puzzle items, and items in general, keeping players on their toes. There's not a lot else to say here. Capcom have REALLY outdone themselves. There's just so much love and care put into this game. You really feel it through every new area you explore, to every puzzle, and with every new "Ooo what's this?" moment you'll experience. It's so rare to play a game now that doesn't feel like it was churned out in a day, and Capcom proves they have they drive to refine their most popular series. 

Unforunately, and this isn't as bad as Dishonored 2 but It has to be brought up, the PC port isn't 100% there. When loading into a new area, the game will slow down to a holt and freeze, sometimes for more than 10 seconds. This KILLED the pace of the game for me sometimes, and I was really disappointed something like that would be in the game. However, im sure Capcom will fix it within the week. It's not [i]that[/i] bad of an issue, as the game will run smooth in almost every other way, but it's still an issue.

My couple of gripes and nitpicks with the game also have to do with the way VHS tapes are handled, enemy variety. So the first VHS tape you stumble upon makes the most logical sense for it to be a VHS tape. It's a couple of guys and they're recording a show for the internet. Now, granted, you're probably not going to record on a camera that can be transfered to the VHS format, but lets ignore that for now. Second VHS is "Mia"... And it really doesn't make sense. Why would Mia be using a camera? How did she get it? Was it Lucas's? If that's the case, why would she be recording anyway? In hopes that Ethan would find the VHS? But how would she get it to him? See, while I enjoy the VHS bits for the change of pace, they don't make sense logically within the story. They're just a way for Capcom to foreshadow certain parts of the level. Buuut... They couldn't think of a more clever way to go about it? The third tape is "Happy Birthday", which doesn't make much sense either, but It doesn't need repeating. The BIGGEST offender to this lapse in logic is the last tape, with Mia on the ship. It plays out more like a flashback than an actual video tape. It's so odd. She's running around, clearly not holding a camera, and at the end she falls into the ocean. How's the tape not damaged? I know... It really is a nitpick, but if this game were less than excellant this kinda off branded thinking about how to exposition to the player would just be real dumb. 

Enemy variety is, again, a semi-small issue. But, I was really hoping for much greater enemy variety than what's in the game currently. There's 4 types of enemies, not counting the multiple boss fights you have with the family, or the bugs. There's the Molded, another Molded but with a big arm, the smaller but faster Molded(admittedly my favorite, because they remind me of Lickers), and lastly the Fat Molded. This more grounded enemy varience certainly helps with the disconnected and more personal feel of the game, but it was kinda dissapointing. When I think of Resident Evil, I think of the multitude of creatures you'll be facing as you progress through the game. It's not really a think you notice or pick up on, because the game paces itself well enough, but I was hoping that with the bayou setting, we'd be seeing local wildlife infected too. Resident Evil games are all about that body horror, but it feels like RE7 is lacking in abundance of it. (Besides the second time you fight Marguerite)

I'll try to keep this short and sweet, and touch on a couple of worries I had that some folks may also have about the game. Keep in mind after finishing the game in 13 hours on Madhouse difficulty I overall felt the game was very good, and I would give it a solid 8.5/10, possibly higher depending on the future content.

No, this game does not just consist of 'run/hide from a monster' like Amnesia, Outlast, SOMA, etc. Puzzles, inventory management, and combat are still present. Similar to previous Resident Evil games (Pre-RE4) you're given a fairly large map to progress through with plenty of simple puzzles, hidden items, and normal enemies similar to zombies in the original mansion. The Baker family is also present, of course. Jack in particular is one of the best antagonists throughout the RE series in my opinion, and it doesn't take much playtime to see why.

The gameplay itsself felt good pretty good with movement, interaction, and guns being straightforward enough for a first person game. I wouldn't say it feels exactly like the older games, but it's very reminiscent of them while being unique. The first-person perspective definitely fits and is handled very well. Another plus? Not a single RE4-6 style quick-time event. Yea, I'm glad they're gone too.

Would I say it's worth $60? Maybe not, it's definitely longer than previous titles, with a possible exception being RE6. It also lacks some post-game content like mercenaries, but it does give you madhouse difficulty and some toys for playthroughs beyond the first. Madhouse difficulty turns off auto-saves almost entirely (save for 1 or 2 sections I believe) and gives you limited saves at designated save points. Additionally, it changes the locations of certain items. Unfortunately, unless you pre-ordered the game madhouse is locked until you finish the game. It's a pretty stupid practice on capcom's part. If you're on the fence about giving RE7 a shot, I'd say pick it up when it's on sale and you'll get an excellent single player game.

Gather around children, and I'll tell you a tale about how a young man who hated horror games was turned around. Yes, and by a small, indie game company with a small, unknown game series. The company's name, Capcom. The series, Resident Evil. You've probably never heard of it. It's pretty underground.

 In all seriousness, I'm not too down on the game. I'd be lying if I said I wasn't scared by it. Resident Evil 7 does a lot right. It's great at building atmosphere and keeps tension high. The sound design is very good; you hear creaks against wood, sloshing of blood and moss, humms of electric appliances, it's wonderful. Not to mention the scares are very authentic through and through. I can recall maybe four or five jump scares in the whole game. I think this game is very worth experiencing, wether it be you playing or watching. Seeing is believing, as they say. Multiple times I said "____ is going to happen, isn't it." And lo and behold, it . . . didn't. The game surprised me with the plot more than once. It felt very fresh, especially considering the state of the series leading up to this installment. (Looking at you Resident Evil 6.)

But, there's one glaring issue I have with the game.

The first half of the game is as described above; scary, immersive, tense, and purely joyful. But the second half makes a shift to more action oriented gameplay. A very, VERY hard shift. Everything I liked about the first half is gone. You go from suspenseful sneaking to a chainsaw fight. I'll say that again: chainsaw fight. You have a chainsaw, and you fight someone else with a chainsaw. Yep. From that point on the combat is . . . okay. I never felt too challenged during fights, especially since the game gives you a machine gun. Horror gets less horrific with a machine gun. Not to mention the fresh, unpredictble plot also shifted. I literally guessed every plot point, successfully spoiling the ending for myself.

Resident Evil 7 went from being an incredibly remarkable game to painfully average in a matter of seconds. I went in expecting to be scared out of my trousers the whole way through. I wasn't. The length is kind of short, though a free expansion is planned for spring this year. It appears combat oriented. Not too sure I'm looking forward to it. Overall, I can't say I recommend this game. I'm not saying it's bad in any way; as said, the first half is magnificent. But the second half is so pitifully boring it made me wish for an ending that never seemed to come. Wait for a sale if you really want it.

Resident Evil 7 paints the series in a whole new light. The experience keeps you on edge throughout the entire game. If anything, I will say that Capcom is moving in the right direction with the Resident Evil series and should continue to strive for immersive horror experiences much like this game has acheived.

Overall, I would give the game an 8 out of 10. While I wish I could give the game a full score, there were some aspects of the game that didn't quite live up to my expectations. The story was amazing, it was very cohesive and progressed at the right speed throughout the entire game. I very much liked the aspect of being able to play various characters and play through the moments of those in the video tapes. The gameplay was good, there were some mechanics that felt clunky, but overall the gameplay meshed as a whole. Boss fights were fun, but the bosses were also annoying, Jack in particular. One thing that I had extremely mixed feelings about was the graphics. I don't consider myself to be a paragon for next gen graphics, but I do expect games like this to provide the highest quality experience, especially considering that this game focuses on photorealism. I found that the graphics were subpar, even on the highest quality. The foliage was significantly low quality, which didn't help to make the experience walking around outside all that great. The very beginning of the game was very akward, transitioning from still photos and 2d foliage to a 3d environment. The indoors were decent however, but occasionally there were some elements in the levels that were out of place, enough to make me cringe.

Altogether I enjoyed the experience and look forward to another playthrough to experience the other ending as well as playing the game on madhouse mode, which will hopefully prove to renew the experience the second time through since most of the jump scare are fairly linear.

When I played the demo, I have to admit that I was skeptical about Resident Evil 7. I am happy to report that my doubts in this game were entirely wrong, this is a brilliant return to survival horror form, and the best entry in the series since the original.

There are so many things that the game did correctly that it's difficult to articulate them all, but the game managed to nail so many of the elements that made classic Resident Evil so great while updating the gameplay to a modern era.

Exploration, item and resource management, puzzles, set pieces, memorable boss fights, tense combat, and a overwhelming sense of atmosphere all come together to form a package that becomes greater than the sum of its parts.

The pacing is perfect, and the story is drip fed to the player just the right amount to encourage play without drowning in exposition.

It took me six hours and fourty five minutes to complete my first playthrough, and I never once felt like the game had overstayed its welcome, I enjoyed every moment of it. For me, it was worth the high price of admission.

If you enjoy true survival horror, I emplore you to buy this game and play it in its entirety alone in a dark room with a pair of headphones. I guarantee that you will enjoy this game, no matter how much you buy it for.
